a25.speaker: Abdullahi Mohamed Ali, herder in Mudug region, Somalia
a25.name: Abdullahi Mohamed Ali
a25.title: herder in Mudug region, Somalia
a25.speech: "The main reason our livestock are dying is the lack of water," he explained. "We relied on small dams, which have run out. The closest water source is Bitaale, 40 km away, where a barrel of water costs $7, which we can't afford." ; Fears their situation will worsen without rain or aid and says these are the worst living conditions he has experienced in his 40 years in the area.

a25.speaker: Burhan Hudi, herder in Mudug region, Somalia
a25.name: Burhan Hudi
a25.title: herder in Mudug region, Somalia
a25.speech: "The livestock are suffering the most from the drought. They don't have enough water or food. The lack of pasture makes them weak. Both people and animals are suffering from this drought," he said. ; "The debts I have are huge. We owe about $5,000. The shops stopped giving us credit. Previously, they gave us food and clothes, but now our animals are dead, and we can't pay our debts," he told Radio Ergo. Plans to relocate his family to a bigger town and is desperate for aid or rain.

a25.speaker: Muhayadi Sheikh Abdi, local district leader in Mudug region
a25.name: Muhayadi Sheikh Abdi
a25.title: local district leader in Mudug region
a25.speech: Confirmed that the lack of water and poor pasture had weakened the livestock, affecting people with no financial reserves. "There is ongoing hunger affecting people and animals. People have lost their livestock and have nowhere to turn. We expect help from God, but there is a great danger to everyone," he warned.

a53.speaker: Molefi Ntseki, South Africa national football team coach
a53.name: Molefi Ntseki
a53.title: South Africa national football team coach
a53.speech: Told SAFA.net ahead of the match that they were to claim the ticket by the time the dust had settled.

a194.speaker: Dr. Anin Ngot Mou, Undersecretary, Ministry of Health (South Sudan), and Ms. Suzanne Mandong, UNFPA South Sudan Representative (op-ed authors)
a194.name: Dr. Anin Ngot Mou
a194.title: Undersecretary, Ministry of Health (South Sudan), and Ms. Suzanne Mandong, UNFPA South Sudan Representative (op-ed authors)
a194.speech: Argue that in South Sudan midwives are not merely responders but critical health system anchors before, during, and after crises, and that they stand as the unsung backbone of survival in a country where maternal mortality remains among the highest globally ; Call for midwives to be systematically included in crisis preparedness, response, and recovery plans and to be decision-makers rather than just service providers, including revising training curricula to include emergency response competencies, guaranteeing decent working conditions and security for midwives in crisis zones, and strengthening intersectoral partnerships ; “Midwives have answered every crisis with courage. Now, it is time the world answers with commitment. Investing in midwives is not optional – it is essential.”

a194.speaker: UNFPA rapid assessment on the role of midwives in humanitarian settings (2023)
a194.name: UNFPA rapid assessment on the role of midwives in humanitarian settings (2023)
a194.speech: Reveals that midwives in South Sudan provide a wide range of frontline sexual, reproductive, maternal, newborn, and adolescent health (SRMNAH) services, even amid the chaos of conflict and natural disasters, including emergency obstetric and newborn care, serving as focal points for reproductive health services in IDP camps, facilitating the Minimum Initial Services Package rollout, championing the rights of women and girls, and providing psychosocial support.

a206.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a206.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.speech: Said they were pleased to receive on behalf of His Majesty's Government the LOX infrastructure installed in key high-volume public hospitals in Eswatini ; "We are also receiving solar infrastructure, which aims to support the efficient supply of oxygen in tertiary facilities and improve service delivery in rural clinics." ; "The infrastructure we are receiving today puts Eswatini in a better position to meet the medical oxygen demands and provide better health services. The infrastructure also ensures that oxygen can be delivered more easily to patients within the hospital wards, with less burden to all those involved in providing oxygen to patients." ; Said the infrastructure also provided significant cost savings to government and that this was an infrastructure that government intended to maintain so it operates efficiently.

a206.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a206.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.speech: Said the provision of this infrastructure by the government was testament of its commitment to ensuring the well-being of the Eswatini nation, and stated that the COVID-19 pandemic exposed significant challenges in accessing and supplying medical oxygen in Eswatini ; "During the peak of the pandemic, our health facilities experienced an overwhelming influx of patients, resulting in a sharp increase in oxygen demand. Our health system struggled to meet these needs, relying heavily on the private sector for the supply of oxygen to our health facilities using cylinders." ; Highlighted that this system proved to be very costly for the Government of Eswatini and frequently led to shortages in oxygen supply: "Therefore, government realised the need to ensure oxygen supply capacity and availability within the country. Therefore, the ministry of health, in collaboration with partners, embarked on strengthening the national oxygen supply."

a206.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a206.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.speech: Said this was all in line with the National Health Sector Strategic Plan and Eswatini National Medical Oxygen Operational Plan, which talk to building sustainable capacity at all levels of the health system to better respond to health emergencies ; "We must bear in mind that medical oxygen is an essential life-saving drug. Oxygen is used among patients at all levels of the healthcare, including in surgery, trauma, heart failure, asthma, pneumonia, and maternal and childcare. It is therefore imperative for the country to ensure the availability and accessibility of adequate and quality medical oxygen to all Emaswati."

a206.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a206.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a206.speech: Added that considering the energy demands to generate oxygen, the ministry also saw the need to come up with a renewable and sustainable source of energy to support this infrastructure: "Solar energy is clean and renewable, reducing grid power usage and reducing air pollution." ; Said this renewable energy had also been expanded to rural health clinics to ensure continuous service delivery for maternal and neonatal care, treatment and screening of patients, and storing vaccines at optimal temperatures to reduce wastage.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said Cape Verde's GDP growth rate, regardless of declarations that express wishes rather than facts, has been low (below 8-9%) and shows a tendency towards stagnation around 4-5%; that the levers of growth have been foreign aid, emigrants' remittances and revenues from tourism and related activities; that at this rate only in 20-25 years will the country reach an income of 10,000 USD per capita while other Small Island Developing States reach 25-30 thousand; that the much-vaunted creation of platforms or hubs and the International Business Centre "are resounding names, but they have not brought the expected results", and that the strategies and their monitors must be revisited.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said national aviation, or rather air connectivity, internal or external, "has not been a success" and much more was expected; that there has been no courage to tackle the real problems with competent and experienced people; that TACV remains a fragile and loss-making company while TAP Air Portugal has been filling the gaps and reinforcing Cape Verde's connectivity via Lisbon, so that "from the much-vaunted hub in Sal, it is we who are being benefited by the Lisbon hub"; that internal air transport needs a complete overhaul; and that the maritime sector has also not been successful, being a drain on public resources because of badly negotiated agreements.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said the privatisation of the Caixa is in fact a reprivatisation, because the shares already belonged to GEO-CAPITAL in the past; that reducing the direct presence of the state in a highly regulated sector is a good signal to the market; that it would be desirable for a foreign bank or financial institution to appear among the new shareholders alongside INPS; and that "the transfer of shares from state ownership to the private sector is always a good sign."

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said that from the point of view of financial proceeds the Public Sale Offering does not change much for the state, involving only about 14 million euros, but that a large public turnout at the Stock Exchange would signal confidence in the country's economy and a change of attitude among Cape Verdeans in placing their savings, while warning "we should not expect a miracle as a result of that" ; said the operation could strengthen the business environment because "it stirs people and can induce a new dynamism in business", since "it is people who make the economy."

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said the amount involved (14 million euros) is small for foreign investment and, given that FDI flows over the last 6-7 years have not performed well, the operation will not have much impact; that it is necessary to analyse what is going well and badly in attracting foreign direct investment and to revive the process.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said Emprofac is perhaps a company with potential for sale if well negotiated and if it effectively reduces medicine prices, but that he would immediately exclude ENAPOR from the published privatisation list; that one should speak not of privatising the ports or their management but of internationalising the ports of Sao Vicente and/or Praia, discussing directly with the 3-5 largest container operators in the Mid-Atlantic region and requiring investments to be at the risk of the candidate.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said the world is passing from a unipolar world dominated by the USA to a multipolar one without clear contours; that by blindly following the USA in its hybrid war against Russia through the instrumentalisation of Ukraine, Europe miscalculated and showed too much subservience and is now suffering the consequences; that Cape Verde, "a passive and confused element in the Western world", suffers from the effects of recession in Europe; that ECOWAS is not and cannot be an alternative for insertion into the world economy; that Cape Verde must remain aligned with and strengthen relations with the USA and the European Union rather than believing China or other Global South countries can leverage its development; that NATO must review its expansionist ambition and concentrate on security in the North Atlantic, where Cape Verde will play an important role at the southern vertex; and that on emigration the country must toughen conditions of establishment and residence and deter clandestine emigrants using Cape Verde as a corridor to Europe.

a261.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.name: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism
a261.title: aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
a261.speech: Said 2024 will be strongly marked by the shock of the third revolution of Social Security (INPS), which by ending the idle and improper exploitation of its unremunerated deposits by part of the national banking sector has awoken to its real mission; that the new policy will improve and increase social benefits and pensions and raise workers' real wages, reducing union pressure for nominal wage increases; and that the INPS positions itself as the central institution on the Cape Verdean economic chessboard, with its helmsman Mario Rui Lopes Fernandes being "the figure of the year".

a361.speaker: Cotton producers of the Commune of Banikoara
a361.name: Cotton producers of the Commune of Banikoara
a361.speech: Are asking the government to right the wrong after an election in which they feel wronged; according to them, there is no question of putting up with this, Banikoara being Benin's largest producing commune, and no question of allowing themselves to be subjugated by the producers of Kandi, who claimed all the good posts on the Board. To show their discontent they emptied the hall and are demanding that this injustice be corrected.

a361.speaker: Confidential sources (anonymous)
a361.name: Confidential sources (anonymous)
a361.speech: According to confidential accounts, the producers of Kandi enjoy the support of the Minister of Agriculture, who is herself originally from Kandi, and she is the puppet-master who in the shadows threw all her weight behind allowing "her own people" to scoop up all the interesting posts on the Board.

a721.speaker: Fortifi Lushima, DRC coordinator of Urgences Panafricanistes
a721.name: Fortifi Lushima
a721.title: DRC coordinator of Urgences Panafricanistes
a721.speech: Commented on these figures for Zone de Contact: “The West has understood one thing. For some time now, they have understood that the whip no longer works with Africans, no longer works with the colonised. So, after slavery and colonisation, they decided to present themselves as humanists, to use humanist values in order to better colonise and better dominate Africans.”

a732.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a732.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a732.speech: Has announced that up to 25 countries are expected to include malaria vaccines in their childhood immunisation programmes by the end of 2025.

a732.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a732.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a732.title: WHO Director-General
a732.speech: Shared the update on Monday during an online media conference focused on global health issues, emphasising that these vaccines could save tens of thousands of young lives annually; raised concerns over the risks posed by recent cuts to US funding for global health initiatives: "Many of the gains in malaria that have been made over the past 20 years are now at risk due to these funding cuts." ; While he refrained from commenting on the US withdrawal from WHO, clarified that the cuts he referred to were those linked to direct US funding, including funding through agencies such as USAID and the US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); warned that the impact is already being felt, with severe disruptions in the supply of malaria diagnostics, medicines, and insecticide-treated nets due to stockouts and delayed deliveries ; "The US has been the largest bilateral donor to the fight against malaria for the past two decades, helping to prevent an estimated 2.2 billion cases and 12.7 million deaths." ; predicted an additional 15 million cases of malaria and 107,000 deaths this year alone if disruptions continue, potentially reversing 15 years of progress.

a732.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a732.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a732.title: WHO Director-General
a732.speech: Noted that with HIV, the suspension of most funding to the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) has halted services for HIV treatment, testing, and prevention in more than 50 countries, and that eight countries are facing severe disruptions to antiretroviral therapy, with some likely to run out of medicine in the coming months; said this could lead to more than 10 million additional cases of HIV and three million HIV-related deaths.

a732.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a732.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a732.title: WHO Director-General
a732.speech: Highlighted the impact on tuberculosis (TB) programmes, with 27 countries in Africa and Asia facing significant disruptions, including shortages of healthcare workers, diagnostic tools, and collapsing data systems, and noted that nine countries have already reported problems with the procurement and supply chains for TB drugs: "Over the past two decades, US support for TB services has saved nearly 80 million lives, but this progress is now at risk."

a732.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a732.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a732.title: WHO Director-General
a732.speech: "Additionally, the WHO's Global Measles and Rubella Network, funded solely by the US, faces an imminent shutdown, just as measles outbreaks are increasing globally. In 2024, 57 large or disruptive measles outbreaks were reported, continuing a trend from the previous three years." ; warned that these cuts are also affecting efforts to eradicate polio, monitor emerging diseases like avian influenza, and respond to disease outbreaks and humanitarian crises, and said nearly 24 million people living in such crises are at risk of losing access to essential health services.

a732.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a732.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a732.title: WHO Director-General
a732.speech: Stressed that other donors must step up, and that countries that have relied on US funding must also increase their domestic health spending to maintain progress in disease control and health services.

a942.speaker: Mamadi Doumbouya, President of Guinea (presidential decree)
a942.name: Mamadi Doumbouya
a942.title: President of Guinea (presidential decree)
a942.speech: Through a decree issued on Tuesday 22 July 2025, appointed several senior officials of the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene as regional inspectors, including Dr. Abdoulaye Sanoh as Regional Director of Health for Conakry and Dr. Abdoulaye Diallo, previously representative of the NGO Prankfinder International in the consortium of the USAID-funded “Notre Santé” project, as Regional Inspector of Health and Public Hygiene of Boké.

a970.speaker: Africa's Pulse, the World Bank's twice-yearly economic update for the region
a970.name: Africa's Pulse
a970.title: the World Bank's twice-yearly economic update for the region
a970.speech: Forecast that growth in Sub-Saharan Africa will fall sharply from 2.4% in 2019 to -2.1 to -5.1% in 2020, the first recession in the region over the past 25 years.

a970.speaker: Hafez Ghanem, World Bank Vice President for Africa
a970.name: Hafez Ghanem
a970.title: World Bank Vice President for Africa
a970.speech: “The COVID-19 pandemic is testing the limits of societies and economies across the world, and African countries are likely to be hit particularly hard.” ; “We are rallying all possible resources to help countries meet people’s immediate health and survival needs while also safeguarding livelihoods and jobs in the longer term – including calling for a standstill on official bilateral debt service payments which would free up funds for strengthening health systems to deal with COVID 19 and save lives, social safety nets to save livelihoods and help workers who lose jobs, support to small and medium enterprises, and food security.”

a970.speaker: The Pulse authors (World Bank report authors)
a970.name: The Pulse authors (World Bank report authors)
a970.speech: Recommend that African policymakers focus on saving lives and protecting livelihoods by focusing on strengthening health systems and taking quick actions to minimize disruptions in food supply chains. They also recommend implementing social protection programs, including cash transfers, food distribution and fee waivers, to support citizens, especially those working in the informal sector.

a970.speaker: Africa's Pulse report (analysis)
a970.name: Africa's Pulse report (analysis)
a970.speech: The analysis shows that COVID-19 will cost the region between $37 billion and $79 billion in output losses for 2020 due to a combination of effects, including trade and value chain disruption; reduced foreign financing flows from remittances, tourism, foreign direct investment, foreign aid, combined with capital flight; and direct impacts on health systems and disruptions caused by containment measures and the public response.

a970.speaker: Africa's Pulse report (on containment challenges)
a970.name: Africa's Pulse report (on containment challenges)
a970.speech: The report points out several factors that pose challenges to the containment and mitigation measures, in particular the large and densely populated urban informal settlements, poor access to safe water and sanitation facilities, and fragile health systems.

a970.speaker: Albert Zeufack, Chief Economist for Africa at the World Bank
a970.name: Albert Zeufack
a970.title: Chief Economist for Africa at the World Bank
a970.speech: “In addition to containment measures, we have seen that in responding to COVID-19, countries are opting for a combination of emergency fiscal and monetary policy actions with many central banks in the region taking important actions like cutting interest rates and providing extraordinary liquidity assistance.” ; “However, it is important to ensure that fiscal policy builds in space for social protection interventions, especially targeting workers in the informal sector, and sows the seed for future resilience of our economies.”

a970.speaker: The authors (of the report)
a970.name: The authors (of the report)
a970.speech: Emphasize the need for a customized policy response to reflect the structure of African economies (especially the large informal sector) and the peculiar constraints policymakers currently face, particularly the deteriorating fiscal positions and heightened public debt vulnerabilities, and the overall low operational capacity to respond.

a970.speaker: Cesar Calderon, Lead Economist and Lead author of the report
a970.name: Cesar Calderon
a970.title: Lead Economist and Lead author of the report
a970.speech: “The immediate measures are important but there is no doubt there will be need for some sort of debt relief from bilateral creditors to secure the resources urgently needed to fight COVID-19 and to help manage or maintain macroeconomic stability in the region.”

a1016.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a1016.name: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a1016.speech: According to UNICEF, the Israeli proposal to open a handful of aid centres exclusively in the south of the Gaza Strip would create an "impossible choice between displacement and death."

a1016.speaker: UNICEF spokesperson (James Elder), at a press briefing in Geneva
a1016.name: UNICEF spokesperson (James Elder)
a1016.title: at a press briefing in Geneva
a1016.speech: Said the plan "contravenes fundamental humanitarian principles" and appears designed to "reinforce control over vital goods as a means of pressure" ; "It is dangerous to ask civilians to go into militarised zones to collect rations... humanitarian aid should never be used as a bargaining chip" ; maintained that Gaza's most vulnerable people - the elderly, disabled children, the sick and the wounded who cannot travel to the designated distribution areas - would face "terrible challenges" in collecting aid ; insisted that the 60 aid trucks a day foreseen by the plan, "one tenth of what was delivered during the ceasefire," is "far from enough to meet the needs of 1.1 million children and 2.1 million people" ; "There is a simple alternative: lift the blockade, let humanitarian aid in, save lives."

a1016.speaker: Humanitarian workers (aid agencies in Gaza)
a1016.name: Humanitarian workers (aid agencies in Gaza)
a1016.speech: Have repeatedly warned that food, water, medicine and fuel were beginning to run out, with the Palestinian enclave under a total aid blockade for more than two months.

a1086.speaker: Numene T. H. Bartekwa, Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.name: Numene T. H. Bartekwa
a1086.title: Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.speech: Has decried unbearable living conditions of citizens in the Southeastern part of the country, particularly Grand Kru County. He said it was time that the Liberian Government erected a checkpoint to the bad road connectivity in the region to halt skyrocketing prices. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, January 21, 2025, at his Capitol Building office, Senator Bartekwa said currently, southeastern Liberia, mainly Grand Kru County, is completely cut off from infrastructure development, investment, and trade due to the lack of roads, something he described as troubling for the region. According to him, there is no road from Sinoe, Maryland, and River Gee to Grand Kru because the roads are closed, thereby leading to prices of commodities on the market in the county to skyrocket, with a 25kg bag of rice now sold for LD$7000-6000, gasoline LD$1,600.

a1086.speaker: Numene T. H. Bartekwa, Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.name: Numene T. H. Bartekwa
a1086.title: Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.speech: Said that, as if that was not enough, the entire county could only boast of fourteen police officers who provided security and responded to crimes, while appealing to the government to pay attention to the suffering of the people of far-to-reach counties.

a1086.speaker: Numene T. H. Bartekwa, Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.name: Numene T. H. Bartekwa
a1086.title: Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.speech: Said the inaccessibility of the county has made it an unfavorable investment destination for investors; investors found in the area are predominantly small-scale and illegal miners. He said that when he engaged investors to invest in the internet, communications, and other commercial banks, people would express interest but would not go due to bad road networks. He says this also applies to people assigned in the county to teach and other civil servants, who usually leave the county and return to Monrovia after employment due to the harsh living conditions.

a1086.speaker: Numene T. H. Bartekwa, Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.name: Numene T. H. Bartekwa
a1086.title: Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.speech: "Our country's development has been delayed for too long, so we have to create a cut-off point. We want to challenge this government to provide the cut-off point and redeem the people from the situation they are faced with. When I was at the lower house, I requested the government, based on the difficulties and constraints our people are going through, to at least muster the courage and credit about US$2 billion to redeem those isolated counties faced with major road challenges," the senator urged. According to him, every rainy season, those counties, especially those from Southeastern Liberia, suffer from road accessibility, infrastructure, and price stability, something he said continues to increase the suffering of the people. He disclosed that with the massive support that the international community is currently trying to provide to Liberia, it's necessary that, first and foremost, the government prioritizes the country's road development infrastructure.

a1086.speaker: Numene T. H. Bartekwa, Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.name: Numene T. H. Bartekwa
a1086.title: Jr., Grand Kru County Senator
a1086.speech: "I want to thank the government of Liberia, headed by President Joseph N. Boakai and his ministers in the economic sector, for their efforts to attract foreign support to the government. As all of you have been following, Liberia was qualified for the MCC compass due to the past government effort, which gave us access to the condition to get US500 million. Also, because of the sustained engagement with IMF, we were told that the government had been given a credit facility of US$200m," he added. According to him, recently, a team from the World Bank was also in country and expressed commitment towards Liberia's energy development sector, something he described as welcoming.

a1086.speaker: World Bank team
a1086.name: World Bank team
a1086.speech: Expressed commitment towards Liberia's energy development sector during a recent visit to the country.

a1254.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO and promoter of the Communication Platform of the African Network of Artisans (speech at the 6th Salon international de l’artisanat des Comores, SIACOM)
a1254.name: Dr Brice Hondi
a1254.title: President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO and promoter of the Communication Platform of the African Network of Artisans (speech at the 6th Salon international de l’artisanat des Comores, SIACOM)
a1254.speech: “Craftsmanship is not a sub-sector. It is not a fallback alternative. Craftsmanship is the silent cradle of our economies. It is the beating heart of our identities. It is the universal genius of our know-how. Alas, it is still one of the most underestimated sectors of our continent.” ; “The observation is blunt: artisans without up-to-date training. Workshops without suitable tools. Masterpieces sold at charity prices. Talents smothered in the informal sector, without social protection or visibility. Meanwhile, our countries import more than 15 billion dollars of craft products every year… WHICH OUR HANDS KNOW HOW TO MAKE BETTER THAN ANYONE. And Africa is impoverished — not for lack of talent, but through neglect.”

a1254.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.name: Dr Brice Hondi
a1254.title: President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.speech: Said that the Communication Platform of the African Network of Artisans, created more than a decade ago, works tirelessly to make the voice of the continent's artisans heard, and that, present in several countries, this initiative carried by the NGO CLUB EXCELLENCE ADECO acts daily to structure, train, connect and promote professionals of the sector: “This platform was not conceived for us, but for you — governments, decision-makers, public actors. Because the challenges of craftsmanship are structurally similar across all our countries. And because only a continental, coherent and sustainable response can meet this challenge.” ; recalled the training cycles initiated in several countries on digitalisation, craft transformation and youth integration, and the events organised to restore artisans' dignity — La Nuit des Artisans since 2014, the Day of African Women Leaders since 2020, and FIMEC since 2024 — announcing that the 2025 edition of FIMEC becomes an international festival with four dimensions: the 2nd FIMEC, the 11th Nuit des Artisans, the 5th Journée des Femmes Leaders Africaines, and the first edition of SIJA (International Symposium of African Youth).

a1254.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.name: Dr Brice Hondi
a1254.title: President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.speech: Addressing Heads of State and Government, saluted the efforts they are already making, but suggested: “Why not devote to craftsmanship a ministry in its own right, with substantial budgets and a continental vision? Why not integrate craft trades into school and university curricula, as a genuine bridge between knowledge and know-how? Why not create an African fund to support craftsmanship and youth entrepreneurship? Why not establish a structural alliance between tourism and craftsmanship, so that what we create finally finds showcases worthy of its genius?” ; “Africa cannot become great by importing its identity. It will become great when it understands the value of what it creates. And that requires that those who create are finally recognised… and taken seriously.”

a1254.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.name: Dr Brice Hondi
a1254.title: President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
a1254.speech: Appealed to the technical and financial partners present or listening: “Support this vision. Join us. This is not an event project. It is a transformation project. A project that touches three vital sectors: craftsmanship, women, youth. To support that is to choose impact, innovation and sustainability.” ; “We seek neither glory nor the spotlight. What we want is that tomorrow a young hairdresser from Burkina, a fashion designer from Malawi, a jeweller from the Comoros… can live with dignity from their art.” ; “What we do not raise up always ends up dying out. Let us not let African craftsmanship die out. Let us make it a torch. A torch of economy, dignity and sovereignty. We have dreamed Africa enough. It is time to build it with our hands.”

a1272.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1272.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1272.speech: has called on Ethiopian authorities to reorient economic policies, citing economic challenges exerted by the Novel Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, locust infestations, and the domestic security situation.

a1272.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1272.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1272.speech: Unlike its earlier projection of flat growth in GDP, the IMF now says Ethiopia's economy will grow by two percent during this fiscal year, with an impressive rebound of 8.7pc the following year. The IMF attributed this outlook to budgetary expansions aimed at offsetting the impact of the pandemic, humanitarian assistance and reconstruction in Tigray, as well as measures in the borrowing and governance of state-owned enterprises. ; Nonetheless, it sees inflationary pressure due to rises in food prices and uncertainty as "ongoing challenges" Ethiopia will continue to face.

a1383.speaker: Sindy Nkuna, data capturer at the Hlokomela Clinic
a1383.name: Sindy Nkuna
a1383.title: data capturer at the Hlokomela Clinic
a1383.speech: On waking up to an email saying that the United States had decided to temporarily freeze all foreign aid in January: "I felt shattered." ; "For days I had racing heartbeats thinking what's going to happen to me and to my kids. It was unbelievable. I have two boys."

a1383.speaker: Sindy Nkuna, data capturer at the Hlokomela Clinic
a1383.name: Sindy Nkuna
a1383.title: data capturer at the Hlokomela Clinic
a1383.speech: Said that since the funding stopped, testing has dropped by nearly 90%.

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: "It affected all of our HIV outreach … it was worse than Covid."

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: Said their latest data from this year shows that Hlokomela has helped the proportion of HIV-infected farm workers to drop to 6.5%.

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: "The fact that we still have a clinic means that we can still do HIV testing. Because if we don't test and get them on treatment, we could have a boom of HIV again." ; "Hopefully we will get another plan. It looks like the Discovery Fund is also going to help us to get the [HIV testing services] HTS going again."

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: On the end of the organisation's main donor funding from the International Organisation for Migration in 2016: "We were worried we were going to close down. One of the challenges was realising there was funder fatigue, so we had to start thinking outside of the box." ; "We found ways to make our own money, got our network of donors to help us find other funders and made an agreement with the provincial health department."

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: Believes registering Hlokomela as an NGO in the US will make it easier to get US funding from philanthropic foundations based there; she says she's been working on the registration for 15 months. "One day we spoke with our managers, and I said we need to get money from America. We started with the application for an NGO in America called the Hlokomela Fund. I just got back from there to finalise it."

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: Says some of the farmers weren't enthusiastic about the co-payment costs, but soon saw the benefits; if they had to take their workers to a government clinic, which was further away, long queues meant they'd have to wait at the clinic all day. According to Du Preez, the new revenue stream brought in around R2 million last year alone.

a1383.speaker: Christine Du Preez, founder of Hlokomela
a1383.name: Christine Du Preez
a1383.title: founder of Hlokomela
a1383.speech: Says that, just as they got through the Covid-19 pandemic without having to let any staff go, they plan to do the same in this crisis. "We've been doing it [outreach HIV testing] for the last 20 years and can't stop now ... There's always a plan B. Don't ask me what it is now, but we'll have one. We always try to have something else."

a1383.speaker: Antoinette Ngwenya, Hlokomela programme manager
a1383.name: Antoinette Ngwenya
a1383.title: Hlokomela programme manager
a1383.speech: Said Hlokomela temporarily transferred two employees from its sex worker programme to help with recording health tracking data, because Nkuna was the only person trained to use the government's HIV database.

a1383.speaker: Antoinette Ngwenya, Hlokomela programme manager
a1383.name: Antoinette Ngwenya
a1383.title: Hlokomela programme manager
a1383.speech: On the organisation's earlier funding from the United Nations International Organisation for Migration: "When we had IOM, we could run many projects and have big events for campaigns. It was great."

a1383.speaker: Hlokomela's managers
a1383.name: Hlokomela's managers
a1383.speech: Argued that some form of co-payment was needed: subsidised services are more sustainable than services which are 100% paid for by donors.

a1383.speaker: South African health department data
a1383.name: South African health department data
a1383.speech: According to health department data, in 2008, 28.5% of farm workers in Hoedspruit had HIV, over 10 percentage points higher than the proportion of adults - 17.64% - who had the virus in South Africa in 2007.

a1486.speaker: Al Jazeera
a1486.name: Al Jazeera
a1486.speech: According to Al Jazeera, during the lunch Trump praised the potential of the African countries and “their valuable lands, with great minerals and great oil deposits.” Al Jazeera writes that Trump is expected to announce shortly the dates for a broader summit with African leaders, possibly in September, around the time of the United Nations General Assembly.

a1486.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1486.name: Donald Trump
a1486.title: US President
a1486.speech: Praised the potential of the African countries and “their valuable lands, with great minerals and great oil deposits.” “There is a lot of anger on your continent. We have managed to resolve a good part of it,” Trump said, pointing to a recent peace agreement signed by the leaders of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda at the White House. ; Trump stated that it is unlikely that the five countries will face American tariffs.

a1486.speaker: White House and Liberian government (statements)
a1486.name: White House and Liberian government (statements)
a1486.speech: According to statements from the White House and from Liberia, the leaders are to discuss key areas of cooperation, including economic development, security, infrastructure and democracy.

a1491.speaker: ‘Maposholi Mosothoane, businesswoman
a1491.name: ‘Maposholi Mosothoane
a1491.title: businesswoman
a1491.speech: Told Public Eye that minister Moteane, in his capacity as a member of the executive, directed the Government Assets Search Recovery Task Team (GASRTT) to intimidate her. “I heard that the GASRTT wanted the gazette to be amended. My question is: why does the team ask me the same questions that Dr Moteane asked me when he filed a case against me? This makes me suspect who the team is working for. Some of the GASRTT members are being used by government officials who sold the site we are fighting over in a bid to hide their nefarious work.” ; According to Mosothoane, Dr Moteane was arrested for fraud relating to the 310 site which the MCC has not classified as his. She also claims that LAA has not registered the site being claimed by Dr Moteane.

a1491.speaker: Government gazette, Declaration of Land Set Aside for Public Purposes at Maseru Central, Maseru City Council (MCC), Notice, 2022
a1491.name: Government gazette
a1491.title: Declaration of Land Set Aside for Public Purposes at Maseru Central, Maseru City Council (MCC), Notice, 2022
a1491.speech: Indicates that a commercial plot No 12284-288 located at Maseru Central, MCC, covering an extent of 2 197 square meters, was leased to one Halemakele Molapo Motšoene; as per the document, it was required for the construction of a fire station, and compensation would also be in the form of land.

a1491.speaker: Maseru City Council (MCC)
a1491.name: Maseru City Council (MCC)
a1491.speech: Said they had not given out plot 12284-310.

a1491.speaker: Tšeliso Makhaphela, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Legal Service (letter to the Commissioner of Police, 4 November 2021)
a1491.name: Tšeliso Makhaphela
a1491.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Director of Legal Service (letter to the Commissioner of Police, 4 November 2021)
a1491.speech: Insisting that MCC should be tasked with the planning for the site: “The Director of Clandestine Survey Services has thus advised that the request for the cancellation of the survey and consolidation of Plot No 12284-228 be made by Maseru City Council as the Planning Authority,” Makhaphela wrote, adding, “The rationale is that this is a planning issue that is within their jurisdiction.”

a1491.speaker: Nkhahle Mosothoane, tenant at the site
a1491.name: Nkhahle Mosothoane
a1491.title: tenant at the site
a1491.speech: Told this paper that Dr Moteane built a wall-like structure that blocked his customers’ cars from entering a car-wash service that is being operated there. “I came in contact with Dr Moteane for about five times; he was meddling in my business, yet I’m just renting the site. This went on until I asked the police for help; he was subsequently arrested and slept at the cell for contempt of court because those issues he was raising were already before the courts,” Nkhahle said. Dr Moteane eventually demolished the wall, allowing customers to pass, according to Nkhahle.

a1491.speaker: Neo Matjato Moteane, Minister of Public Works of Lesotho
a1491.name: Neo Matjato Moteane
a1491.title: Minister of Public Works of Lesotho
a1491.speech: Hit back by saying that Mosothoane was “barking at the wrong tree…I will do my job even if it is my relative involved. I was recently there, (where the fire station) will be constructed; I do not know what she is talking about. Why would I be abusing my power? What she does not know is that I am a loyal servant of His Majesty (King Letsie III),” a furious Moteane said, adding, “I condemn with the strongest terms assertions she is making about me.”

a1491.speaker: Dr Mohlalefi Moteane
a1491.name: Dr Mohlalefi Moteane
a1491.speech: Told this publication that he is not interested in discussing the issue, thus, “I am keeping quiet.”

a1491.speaker: Advocate Seeng Matšosa, GASRTT chairperson
a1491.name: Advocate Seeng Matšosa
a1491.title: GASRTT chairperson
a1491.speech: Confirmed that on February 3 this year, they went to the site in which Mosothoane and Dr Moteane are fighting over but denied allegations that they are fighting politicians’ battles. “The purpose of our visit was to hear issues related to the place, as it is our mandate as a team. We met with the police, where we discussed matters related to the project,” Matšosa said.

a1491.speaker: ‘Makatleho Mosala, MCC Public Relations Manager
a1491.name: ‘Makatleho Mosala
a1491.title: MCC Public Relations Manager
a1491.speech: Told this publication that even though they are not privy to the happenings at the site in question, as far as she knows it has always been their property, “but I will revert on that issue later.”

a1491.speaker: Senior Superintendent Mpiti Mopeli, police information officer
a1491.name: Senior Superintendent Mpiti Mopeli
a1491.title: police information officer
a1491.speech: Said they are forging ahead with construction of the fire brigade building as planned. “I am not aware of the letter from the LAA you are asking about, but it’s all systems go from our side regarding the building for the fire station,” Mopeli said.

a1491.speaker: Hopolang Lenoesa, Land Administration Authority (LAA) Information Officer
a1491.name: Hopolang Lenoesa
a1491.title: Land Administration Authority (LAA) Information Officer
a1491.speech: “In 2023 there was mediation, which failed to resolve their squabble, as for us as the LAA, we had to set aside our efforts since they (Mosothoane and Dr Moteane) decided to head to courts of law,” Lenoesa said. Lenoesa highlighted that she cannot say whether Dr Moteane’s site has not been registered as claimed by Mosothoane since the matter is sub judice.

a1635.speaker: Ebrima Sillah, Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.name: Ebrima Sillah
a1635.title: Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.speech: Has said government's vision extends beyond ports and airports, but also to the revitalisation of river transport, which he said is crucial for connecting communities and promoting trade along the River Gambia. "So, I am pleased to announce our ongoing collaboration with the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) to revive river transport systems, which will unlock significant economic potential for riverine communities and beyond."

a1635.speaker: Ebrima Sillah, Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.name: Ebrima Sillah
a1635.title: Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.speech: Said The Gambia is witnessing an "impressive expansion" of its road infrastructure, anchored on the OIC Roads Project being "progressively implemented" to improve accessibility, reduce travel times, and enhance economic activities ; said government is also going into "asset recycling" in order to unlock the value of existing infrastructure assets to finance new projects and accelerate development without increasing public debt.

a1635.speaker: Ebrima Sillah, Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.name: Ebrima Sillah
a1635.title: Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.speech: On green infrastructure solutions: "Our focus on sustainable infrastructure also includes the introduction of Green Ferries, with support from the African Development Bank (AfDB). These ferries will reduce carbon emissions and improve transportation efficiency across the River Gambia, supporting our commitment to a greener, more sustainable future."

a1635.speaker: Ebrima Sillah, Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.name: Ebrima Sillah
a1635.title: Gambian Minister of Transport, Works and Infrastructure
a1635.speech: Said development infrastructure is not just about roads, bridges, and ports but the foundation upon which we build sustainable economic growth and social prosperity. "In The Gambia, it is important to state that accelerating infrastructure development is at the very heart of our Green Focused National Development Plan (NDP) 2022-2027. The new NDP Program known as YIRIWA, is designed to spur growth, enhance productivity, and foster inclusive development. One of the key pillars of the YIRIWA agenda is to transform the seaport of Banjul into a regional logistics hub through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). We are currently exploring opportunities to upgrade and modernise the port's facilities to boost trade, enhance efficiency, and place The Gambia as a strategic gateway to the sub-region. Government is also at an advanced stage in project preparation and design to build a new deep-sea port in Sanyang in the Kombo South region of Western Gambia that will serve as a game changer and firmly position The Gambia as a logistic hub in the West Africa region."

a1749.speaker: United Nations
a1749.name: United Nations
a1749.speech: Announced on Thursday the release of $110 million to offset "the precipitous decline" in funding devoted to humanitarian aid worldwide, particularly in Africa ; said one third of the allocated funds will go to supporting the humanitarian response in Sudan, plunged into civil war since April 2023 and currently experiencing the world's worst humanitarian crisis, as well as in neighbouring Chad, which hosts a large number of refugees fleeing the violence, with funds also distributed among countries such as Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Honduras, Mauritania, Niger, Somalia, Venezuela and Zambia ; said the recent funding cuts are creating a global funding crisis that threatens the lives of millions of children.

a1749.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1749.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1749.speech: Said the emergency funds of $110 million from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) aim to strengthen life-saving assistance in ten of the most underfunded and neglected crises, notably in Africa, Asia and Latin America ; warned that although more than 300 million people worldwide are expected to depend on humanitarian aid in 2025, funding is declining every year and "This year's levels are expected to reach a historic low."

a1749.speaker: Tom Fletcher, Emergency Relief Coordinator and head of OCHA (statement)
a1749.name: Tom Fletcher
a1749.title: Emergency Relief Coordinator and head of OCHA (statement)
a1749.speech: "For countries hit by conflict, climate change and economic turmoil, brutal funding cuts do not mean that humanitarian needs disappear."

a1749.speaker: Catherine Russell, Executive Director of UNICEF
a1749.name: Catherine Russell
a1749.title: Executive Director of UNICEF
a1749.speech: "Millions of children are affected by conflict, must be vaccinated against deadly diseases such as measles and polio, and must be educated and kept healthy."

a1749.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1749.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1749.speech: Warned that funding cuts, particularly the freeze on American disbursements decided by the Trump administration, threaten the progress made in the fight against tuberculosis, the world's deadliest infectious disease; said global efforts against tuberculosis have saved more than 79 million lives over the past two decades but these gains are now threatened by budget cuts, with Washington having traditionally provided about $200 to $250 million a year to fight the disease.

a1953.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a1953.name: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a1953.speech: Announced that it is accepting new applications for the Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) program, that anyone, anywhere can apply at any time, and set out the tiered funding structure – Stage-One grants (up to USD200,000), Stage-Two grants (USD200,000 to USD1,500,000), Stage-Three grants (USD1,500,000 to USD5,000,000) and separate evidence grants (up to USD1,500,000); it stated that since 2010, DIV has invested in over 190 solutions across 46 countries and all sectors in which USAID invests, has directly affected more than 30 million lives, that over half of DIV grantees had never received USAID funding before, and that DIV has mobilized USD4.60 of external funding for every USD1 from the American people.

a1974.speaker: Akua Donkor, founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.name: Akua Donkor
a1974.title: founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.speech: At an Inter Party Advisory Committee (IPAC) meeting in Accra two weeks ago, expressed her unhappiness with what she termed as derogatory comments about her qualifications as a presidential candidate for Election 2024; she was particularly not happy with what she said was the continuous derogatory remarks about her qualification as a presidential candidate, considering that she was not educated in a classroom.

a1974.speaker: Akua Donkor, founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.name: Akua Donkor
a1974.title: founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.speech: Promised to provide free education from primary to secondary level, erase import taxes and establish a free zone at the Tema Port to attract businesses as well as buy vehicles for all practising journalists in the country; she also wanted to change the maternity leave for women from its original three months to one year to provide enough time for the nursing mother to take proper care of herself.

a1974.speaker: Akua Donkor, founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.name: Akua Donkor
a1974.title: founder and leader of the Ghana Freedom Party (GFP)
a1974.speech: Over the years she had expressed regret that some women went to jail for defaulting on a loan; she advocated that it was when they did not make good sales and did not earn enough that they were unable to repay the loans, and those women, she said, ended up in prison, leaving behind their husbands and children; said she would make sure that women who had been jailed under those circumstances were released to return to their families if she was elected President in the December election ; “I will then give them loans and give them three years before they settle their loans. This way, they will be able to use the money efficiently and earn enough to be able to repay the loans.”

a2061.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission chief
a2061.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a2061.title: African Union Commission chief
a2061.speech: “I wish to commend the crucial role played by Qatar, Egypt & the USA.”

a2061.speaker: South Africa (Foreign Ministry statement)
a2061.name: South Africa (Foreign Ministry statement)
a2061.speech: Welcoming the pact, called for the implementation of a “just and lasting peace that ensures the human rights of both Palestinians and Israelis are protected and promoted” ; “The ceasefire agreement is a crucial first step toward ending the severe humanitarian crisis faced by the 2.3 million Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, which the International Court of Justice (ICJ) has deemed to be plausibly genocidal” ; the cease-fire “must lay the basis for a just peace which should include the establishment of a contiguous, independent, and viable Palestinian state” ; “Palestinian sovereignty and territorial integrity must be upheld. It is imperative that no land is annexed in either Gaza or the West Bank following the cease-fire, and that illegal settlement expansion is halted” ; said the successive rulings and provisional measures of the top UN court “must be adhered to by the occupying power. International law and humanitarian law must be respected and upheld.”

a2061.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a2061.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a2061.title: President of Somalia
a2061.speech: Commended the efforts of Qatar, Egypt, and the US in brokering the agreement; emphasized the importance of sustaining the cease-fire and urged the international community to expedite the delivery of urgent humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza: “With this agreement, I stress the need for collective efforts to stabilize the ceasefire and prioritize the swift provision of humanitarian assistance to alleviate the suffering in Gaza,” he said in a statement issued by the presidency on Thursday.

a2061.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a2061.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a2061.title: President of Somalia
a2061.speech: Underscored the necessity of establishing an independent and sovereign Palestinian state based on the two-state solution.

a2061.speaker: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Qatari Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs
a2061.name: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman
a2061.title: Qatari Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs
a2061.speech: Announced the success of mediators in reaching a cease-fire agreement in the Gaza Strip, noting that its implementation will begin this Sunday.

a2203.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.name: Abiy Ahmed
a2203.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.speech: Used the phrase "African solutions to African problems" seven times during his speech delivered on February 18, and offered the suggestion that existing conflicts and disputes on the continent must be resolved through collective efforts and "must be confined to this continent and quarantined from the contamination of non-African interference."

a2203.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.name: Abiy Ahmed
a2203.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.speech: Emphasized that while leaders are looking for external investment, much should be based on practical and valuable investment, and that Africa needs to improve its economy and look towards attaining economic sovereignty.

a2203.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.name: Abiy Ahmed
a2203.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2203.speech: On food security and food sovereignty, said "While the principle of African Solutions to African Problems is widely raised in the scope of conflict, it is imperative that we begin to extend this principle to a wide range of peace and security issues. Our continent is not only well able to feed itself, but can become a bread basket of the world. With 65% of the world's remaining uncultivated arable land in our backyards, we need to critically assess why one third of the hungry people in the world are in our continent." ; called upon the African Union and development partners to offer investment support in unleashing this potential ; "Sadly, the principle of African Solutions to African Problems is not a silver bullet to address all challenges, because not all our problems are the products of our own making."

a2203.speaker: 2023 Dakar Declaration on Food Sovereignty and Resilience
a2203.name: 2023 Dakar Declaration on Food Sovereignty and Resilience
a2203.speech: Acknowledged the continental awakening that 'it is time for Africa to feed itself and fully unlock its agriculture potential to feed the world'.

a2203.speaker: Macky Sall, Senegalese President and Former AU Chairperson; Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission executive leader; and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
a2203.name: Macky Sall
a2203.title: Senegalese President and Former AU Chairperson; Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission executive leader; and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
a2203.speech: Have strongly been advocating Africa's inclusion on foreign bodies, lending their voices yet again for Africa to be represented on the UN Security Council with at least one permanent seat and double non-permanent seats, and for proportionate representation at the G7, the G20 and similar international institutions.

a2395.speaker: Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: Has said it will work aggressively on public relation and communication in the region to separate the people from the TPLF, since the people of Tigray have been very close and highly attached to the TPLF ; said it has finalized its charter to re-establish new Regional and Zone cabinet structures, while Woreda councils and Kebele administration will continue.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: “The Tigray people have been hostage of the TPLF for many years. One of the important work the interim administration will be involved in is the rehabilitation work on cooperating with the federal government to ensure justice and good governance widens the political space in the region by involving all political parties.” ; “The political space in the region has been very narrow. So we will open up this and invite all political parties, groups and individuals to operate by respecting the rule of law.” ; Noted TPLF will not be allowed to participate in the new administration, since high officials and executive bodies are engaged in the crime and the so called illegal election.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: Said in his media briefing on Thursday that provisional administration will be instituted in the areas liberated from the TPLF.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: “The establishment of the interim administration aims to ensuring the benefits of the People of Tigray and sustain lasting peace by restructuring the preceding administration system.” ; Noted the new administration will establish a task force to investigate the case of individuals in custody in the Tigray region ; Noted the Tigriyan people have been suffering from lack of justice and good governance, adding that the interim administration will work to create an enabling situation whereby these problems could be tackled.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: Added that the interim administration will discharge its responsibility in facilitating credible and participatory elections to be held in Tigray Regional State ; “Making smooth transition and conducting free and legal election are the main targets of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State,” adding that the people of Tigray have been coerced into unfair and illegal elections by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) for years.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: According to him, the immediate action will be resuming social services not properly functioning at the moment, including education, health and so forth, in collaboration with the federal government, sector ministries and other stakeholders.

a2395.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.name: Mulu Nega
a2395.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a2395.speech: Regarding the relation with Eritrea, said: “We will try to restore peace and stability with neighboring regions and Eritrea. There is some mistrust. So our task is to restore peace and stability within Tigray as well as with neighboring regions and the Eritrean government.”

a2395.speaker: Ethiopia (government)
a2395.name: Ethiopia (government)
a2395.speech: Has said its forces are bearing down on the capital of Tigray region, in a two-week-old war that has killed hundreds and forced 30,000 refugees to flee into neighboring Sudan.

a2395.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.name: Redwan Hussein
a2395.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.speech: “Our defense forces are moving forward and closing in on Mekelle,” he told reporters. “There are a number of towns that have fallen,” he added.

a2395.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.name: Redwan Hussein
a2395.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.speech: Informs the Capital newspaper that countries, including the United Nations, were evacuating their citizens and staffs from the Tigray region, and that hundreds of foreign aid workers have left Tigray through boarders of Afar. He said the regional government is protecting them from Mekelle to the border of Afar State through their satellite communications; all organizations must provide a list of people to be evicted and ensure that they are not wanted for crime; and the government is seeking better conditions for humanitarian assistance to the United Nations to alleviate the living conditions in the Tigray region.

a2395.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.name: Redwan Hussein
a2395.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a2395.speech: Said the government has organized two groups of fact finding missions to assess the situation on the ground on both the western and east southern parts of the region to find which way is easy to supply humanitarian assistance, and that there is a plan to bring back the migrants from neighboring countries.

a2471.speaker: Sanlam Group Awards organisers (statement)
a2471.name: Sanlam Group Awards organisers (statement)
a2471.speech: Said this year's award attracted 237 entries from 17 countries across the African continent, noting it is the highest entries ever in the competition's 50-year history ; "87 entries were from South Africa while 150 entries were submitted from other countries, including Egypt, Nigeria, Morocco, Kenya, Ghana, and Uganda," the statement said.

a2471.speaker: Sanlam Group Awards organisers
a2471.name: Sanlam Group Awards organisers
a2471.speech: According to the organisers, the work of the finalists represents the best financial journalism in Africa, reporting on the continent's challenges and progress in business, trade and economics, ESG in relation to business and the environment, and ESG in relation to business and social impact.

a2471.speaker: Nixon Kariithi, professor and chair of the judging panel
a2471.name: Nixon Kariithi
a2471.title: professor and chair of the judging panel
a2471.speech: Said the judges were impressed by the quality of the work produced by journalists across the continent ; "This is most pleasing at a moment when there is greater international attention on Africa as global summits such as the G20 are set to take place on the continent for the first time."

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: “We have a twofold objective: to ensure water quality but also to disinfect the water that is consumed” ; recounts that their research found the main cause of diarrhoeal diseases in Burundi, especially in the Imbo plain, is the consumption of contaminated water.

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: Said a 2019 GIZ study shows that 25% of water sources are contaminated by bacteria: “And at household level, contamination reached up to 75% of cases. That means water can be contaminated during transport and storage. All along the supply chain.” ; indicated that in rural areas the water consumed is not treated, that 76% of rural households have access to water that does not come from piped systems where there is no reservoir, that disinfection in such conditions becomes very complicated, whereas in cities such as Bujumbura the water is treated and disinfected.

a2625.speaker: GIZ study (2019)
a2625.name: GIZ study (2019)
a2625.speech: Shows that 25% of water sources are contaminated by bacteria.

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: Described the production process: “First, we measure the raw material (sodium chloride) that is needed for production, then we weigh it with the analytical balance. After that, we pour the product into a carefully measured volume of water and that produces electrolysis, the passage of electricity through the solution” ; “When the maximum concentration is reached, we stop” ; “And there, we use a reagent and we take a sample, etc. We shake it. After a certain time, the colour changes. The number of drops we have put into the solution is proportional to the concentration of chlorine in terms of grams per litre” ; specified that the pH of the solution after stabilisation must be between 9.5 and 10.5 and that the concentration must remain unchanged for between 6 and 9 months ; “These jerrycans must be labelled, specifying the production date, the expiry date, etc.”

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: Mentioned that importing five litres of chlorine costs more than 10,000 BIF: “Whereas the cost of local production of the same quantity is close to 5,000 BIF. A saving of almost 50%.”

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: Said two approaches are used to disinfect water: the first consists of installing a chlorine dispenser next to a water point or borehole; the other is the cleaning and disinfection of reservoirs — “It is used where there are piped water systems, where there are reservoirs, collection chambers... After cleaning, the chlorine is added according to the volume of water found in that reservoir and in the piping” ; noted they also monitor water quality: “We must make sure that the disinfected water has a good concentration of residual chlorine within the standards recommended by the WHO, but also measure the microbiological quality of the water that the population is using.”

a2625.speaker: Olivier Nihimbazwe, initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.name: Olivier Nihimbazwe
a2625.title: initiator of the Water for Development project
a2625.speech: Indicated that to carry out this work they use funds from various prizes won in national and international competitions, including the D-Prize Global Competition (2020), the Swiss Water Partnership Youth Water Challenge (2021), Global Youth Mobilisation (2022) and the Global Greengrants Fund (2022).

a2625.speaker: Residents of Rukana II hill
a2625.name: Residents of Rukana II hill
a2625.speech: According to the residents, the other boreholes installed there have been dry for years.

a2625.speaker: Willy Ndayishimiye, member of the Water for Development team
a2625.name: Willy Ndayishimiye
a2625.title: member of the Water for Development team
a2625.speech: Insists that every person who comes to draw water at the source must make sure their jerrycan or container is properly washed: “After that, they will just turn the valve to let a few millilitres of chlorine flow out, with a well-defined dose to be able to treat their volume of water.”

a2625.speaker: Willy Ndayishimiye, member of the Water for Development team
a2625.name: Willy Ndayishimiye
a2625.title: member of the Water for Development team
a2625.speech: Laments about school hygiene: “Improving hygiene conditions in schools is also our concern. We have observed that there are children who eat without washing their hands because there is no handwashing facility or no water.”

a2625.speaker: Carine Kanyange, resident of Rukana II hill
a2625.name: Carine Kanyange
a2625.title: resident of Rukana II hill
a2625.speech: “We were really very unhappy. No drinking water in our area. We were forced to consume this dirty water, without any treatment” ; states that their lives were in danger: “It is this water that we used for laundry, cooking and drinking. Our children and the adults often suffer from intestinal worms and other dirty-hands diseases. And this is because of the poor quality of the water we consume” ; hopes that with the disinfection of the water their health will improve, and states that today everyone is obliged to disinfect the water.

a2625.speaker: Oscar Bukuru, resident of the locality
a2625.name: Oscar Bukuru
a2625.title: resident of the locality
a2625.speech: Appreciates the initiative and does not hide that the water was very dirty: “Look, there are even small fish in the water. That shows it is not drinkable. But we have no other choice.” For him, it is because of this water that cholera cases are often identified; he has no doubt that with disinfection such cases, including intestinal worms, will decline.

a2625.speaker: Léonce Nzikwinkunda, president of the communal water authority (Régie communale de l’eau) of Rugombo
a2625.name: Léonce Nzikwinkunda
a2625.title: president of the communal water authority (Régie communale de l’eau) of Rugombo
a2625.speech: Judges the project beneficial: “These young people help us a lot. Because our region, our commune, cruelly lacks drinking water. Yet the distribution of good-quality water is the source of good health.”

a2625.speaker: Léonce Nzikwinkunda, president of the communal water authority (Régie communale de l’eau) of Rugombo
a2625.name: Léonce Nzikwinkunda
a2625.title: president of the communal water authority (Régie communale de l’eau) of Rugombo
a2625.speech: Reports that drinking water is insufficient in Rugombo commune: “We currently have three water networks” — Ruzibira-Rukana, Nyakabingo-Kiramira and Kagobajana-Rusororo, with a total flow of 13 litres per second, which he explains is insignificant; he calls for an increase in the number of water networks in his commune: “The construction of the Nyaruseke-Rukana network, which is half-completed, must be finished.”

a2655.speaker: Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of the Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO)
a2655.name: Edmund Yakani
a2655.title: Executive Director of the Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO)
a2655.speech: Is calling for urgent support to help thousands of internally displaced people who recently returned to South Sudan from Uganda. Says displaced families in Panyume Payam of Morobo County are living in very poor conditions, without enough humanitarian assistance; says the situation in Panyume is dire. “I would like to take this opportunity with tears falling out of my eye and with worries and with disturbance in my heart to see the South Sudanese population in Morobo county,” he said. “Look at what we have done to our own people whom we claimed that one day we will govern them as leaders. Our citizens are suffering as if their vote for independence was a curse,” he lamented.

a2655.speaker: Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of CEPO
a2655.name: Edmund Yakani
a2655.title: Executive Director of CEPO
a2655.speech: Says the people are suffering and need urgent help. He’s appealing for donations of second-hand clothes, iron sheets, and medical assistance to help families affected by the crisis. “I am appealing to South Sudanese of good wishers that CEPO as an organization we have launched a campaign to assist this population with second hand clothes and whatever you can contribute, and if they are any other people who are ready to volunteer with this community in terms of medical services we appeal to you,” he stated. The activist says the campaign will continue in the coming weeks and is asking the public and humanitarian organizations to respond to the emergency in Morobo.

a2655.speaker: Vita Henry, journalist working with Morobo FM
a2655.name: Vita Henry
a2655.title: journalist working with Morobo FM
a2655.speech: Said the group had been living in refugee camps but decided to move out due to worsening conditions and cuts in food aid. According to him, insecurity along the border increased in recent weeks, prompting the Ugandan army to carry out a three-day operation; during the operation, many refugees were removed and transported to a camp by lorries.

a3174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3174.name: Donald Trump
a3174.title: US President
a3174.speech: raised on Monday the possibility that Ukraine might become "Russian one day", demanding that the aid paid to Kyiv be compensated ; repeated on Fox News that he wanted to obtain access to Ukrainian rare earths, explaining that Washington had to "secure" the money paid out given the uncertainty over the outcome of the conflict ; "They could reach a deal, they could not reach a deal. They could be Russian one day, or they could not be Russian one day" ; "I want to get back" that money, adding that he had demanded from Kyiv the equivalent of 500 billion dollars' worth of rare earths. "At least that way we don't feel stupid." ; pledged to put a swift end to the "carnage".

a3174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3174.name: Donald Trump
a3174.title: US President
