a3174.speech: confirmed a visit to Ukraine on 20 February by his special envoy, Keith Kellogg, tasked with drawing up a plan to end the conflict.

a3174.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a3174.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3174.title: President of Ukraine
a3174.speech: had assured last week that his country was ready to receive "investments from American companies" in its rare earths, stressing however that "part of our mineral resources" is located in occupied territory.

a3174.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a3174.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3174.title: President of Ukraine
a3174.speech: indicated on Monday that the organisation of a meeting with Mr Trump was under way, but that the date had not yet been set.

a3174.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a3174.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3174.title: President of Ukraine
a3174.speech: called on Monday for "a real peace and effective security guarantees" for Ukraine ; declared at the beginning of the month that he was ready for direct negotiations with Mr Putin, "if that is the only configuration in which we can bring peace to the citizens of Ukraine and stop losing people" ; long rejected the idea of negotiations, saying he wanted to defeat Russia on the battlefield.

a3174.speaker: Ukrainian presidency
a3174.name: Ukrainian presidency
a3174.speech: According to the Ukrainian presidency, Volodymyr Zelensky will be present on Friday at the Munich Security Conference (MSC), where he will meet American vice-president J.D. Vance.

a3174.speaker: Christoph Heusgen, president of the Munich Security Conference (MSC)
a3174.name: Christoph Heusgen
a3174.title: president of the Munich Security Conference (MSC)
a3174.speech: announced to the press that besides Mr Vance, Mr Kellogg and Secretary of State Marco Rubio will be part of the American delegation.

a3174.speaker: German Galushchenko, Ukrainian energy minister
a3174.name: German Galushchenko
a3174.title: Ukrainian energy minister
a3174.speech: reported on Facebook a Russian attack "on the country's gas infrastructure", adding that electricity supplies had been limited in order to "minimise the potential consequences for the energy sector".

a3174.speaker: Ukrainian army
a3174.name: Ukrainian army
a3174.speech: triggered air alerts during the night in several areas of the country, citing threats from drones and ballistic weapons.

a3174.speaker: Local authorities (Ukraine)
a3174.name: Local authorities (Ukraine)
a3174.speech: reported strikes in several regions including Zaporizhzhia (east), Poltava (centre-east), and Dnipropetrovsk (east), reporting several injured.

a3174.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a3174.name: Vladimir Putin
a3174.title: President of Russia
a3174.speech: has said several times that he is ready to negotiate, on condition that Ukraine bows to his demands: ceding four regions of the south and east of the country, in addition to Crimea annexed in 2014, and renouncing joining NATO.

a3174.speaker: The New York Post
a3174.name: The New York Post
a3174.speech: had reported on Saturday a telephone conversation between Mr Trump and Mr Putin.

a3174.speaker: Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman
a3174.name: Dmitry Peskov
a3174.title: Kremlin spokesman
a3174.speech: refused to confirm or deny the exchange between Trump and Putin.

a3349.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3349.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3349.speech: Said on Saturday that a four-year-old child became the second person to die of Ebola in Uganda since the outbreak was announced in late January.

a3349.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3349.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3349.speech: Said it and others were working to strengthen contact tracing together with surveillance, contact tracing being key to stemming the spread of Ebola.

a3349.speaker: Ugandan health officials
a3349.name: Ugandan health officials
a3349.speech: Confirmed on Tuesday that the country had recorded 10 infections with the Sudan strain of the virus.

a3480.speaker: Umaro Sissoco Embalo, President of Guinea-Bissau
a3480.name: Umaro Sissoco Embalo
a3480.title: President of Guinea-Bissau
a3480.speech: Presented his vision of a Guinea-Bissau that is "stable, secure and open to foreign investment", highlighting the priority sectors of energy, agriculture, tourism, technology and infrastructure, with the country's new investment code presented as a key tool for attracting solid partnerships.

a3480.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a3480.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a3480.title: President of Senegal
a3480.speech: Presented his "new vision of cooperation based on trade, mutually beneficial investment and respect for reciprocal interests", highlighting Senegal's many assets, notably its political stability, its attractive business climate and its strategic geographical position.

a3480.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a3480.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a3480.title: President of Senegal
a3480.speech: At an executive round table at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce bringing together some thirty senior American business leaders, set out his "clear, bold and attractive" economic vision for Senegal, particularly highlighting the reforms undertaken to significantly improve the business climate and investment opportunities in key sectors: energy, agri-food industry, infrastructure, the digital economy and natural resources (oil and gas).

a3480.speaker: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
a3480.name: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
a3480.speech: Announced the forthcoming publication of an Investment Guide dedicated specifically to Senegal.

a3480.speaker: Christopher Landau, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State and Chairman of the Board of the DFC
a3480.name: Christopher Landau
a3480.title: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State and Chairman of the Board of the DFC
a3480.speech: Expressed the firm willingness of the United States to strengthen its economic cooperation with Senegal through more investment and increased collaboration between the private sectors of the two countries.

a3480.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a3480.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a3480.title: President of Liberia
a3480.speech: Expressed Liberia's gratitude for the historic partnership with the United States, declaring: "Liberia is a long-standing friend of the United States, and we believe in your vision of making America great again."

a3480.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a3480.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a3480.title: President of Liberia
a3480.speech: Called for strengthened collaboration in the mining sector and requested support to carry out exhaustive mineral surveys, declaring: "Liberia possesses vast mineral potential and, as a trusted friend, we are seeking support to carry out exhaustive mineral surveys. This is essential to unlock sustainable growth and mutual economic benefits." ; In his bilateral meeting with President Trump, invited the United States Geological Survey (USGS) to partner with Liberia to carry out a national mapping of critical minerals, aimed at identifying strategic investment opportunities in rare earth elements, lithium and other essential minerals.

a3480.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a3480.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a3480.title: President of Liberia
a3480.speech: Stressed Liberia's commitment to transparency, good governance and the rule of law, presenting his flagship ARREST programme (Agriculture, Roads, Rule of law, Education, Sanitation and Tourism) as a framework for economic partnership and growth.

a3480.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia (speaking through Ambassador Charles A. Snetter Jr.)
a3480.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a3480.title: President of Liberia (speaking through Ambassador Charles A. Snetter Jr.)
a3480.speech: Called on American and international investors to seize new investment opportunities, declaring: "Gone are the days of mere PowerPoint presentations, we are now on the ground, taking tangible action. We invite you to take part in this transformation." ; Also stressed the importance of Liberia's unanimous election to a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, calling it a "powerful testimony to Liberia's growing international credibility - and a signal to investors around the world that Liberia is back and open for business."

a3480.speaker: Christopher Landau, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
a3480.name: Christopher Landau
a3480.title: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
a3480.speech: Welcomed the recent signing of the concession and access agreement (CAA) with Ivanhoe Liberia Ltd., guaranteeing multi-user access to Liberia's essential rail corridor.

a3480.speaker: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, President of Gabon
a3480.name: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema
a3480.title: President of Gabon
a3480.speech: Presented his vision of "building a strong, sovereign and forward-looking economy", particularly highlighting the emblematic 901 km Belinga-Boue-Mayumba railway project, intended to transport iron ore and to structure the national territory, alongside other structuring projects: an agreement with Millenial Potash for the Mayumba potash, discussions with ExxonMobil and Boeing, the Mayumba deep-water port, the Boue hydroelectric dam and financing requests to the US-DFC and EXIMBANK.

a3480.speaker: American investors (at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce meeting with Gabon)
a3480.name: American investors (at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce meeting with Gabon)
a3480.speech: Welcomed the reforms undertaken in Gabon and expressed their willingness to support these ambitious projects.

a3480.speaker: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani, President of Mauritania
a3480.name: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani
a3480.title: President of Mauritania
a3480.speech: Expressed his "deep gratitude for the invitation" and appreciated "the American president's efforts to bring peace to several regions" ; welcomed President Trump's peace efforts, noting "the need to work to end the war in the Gaza Strip" and stressing that his administration "has played an important role in establishing peace" in various regions.

a3480.speaker: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani, President of Mauritania
a3480.name: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani
a3480.title: President of Mauritania
a3480.speech: Stressed "the great potential Mauritania has with its strategic position, on the Atlantic Ocean coast, adjacent to the United States, as well as the creation of a link between North Africa and South Africa" ; recalled that "for sixty years, Mauritania has remained the second-largest producer of iron ore in Africa and that its sea water is rich in resources, particularly fish."

a3770.speaker: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI) (2022 report)
a3770.name: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI) (2022 report)
a3770.speech: Has reported that although the country earned over US$1.63 billion from its legal extractive sector between 2009 and 2021, a substantial portion of the country's actual mineral output is never taxed or recorded; and that as much as 90% of Liberia's gold production is believed to be smuggled out of the country, contributing to annual revenue losses estimated between US$150 million to US$450 million.

a3770.speaker: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI) and the Ministry of Mines and Energy
a3770.name: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI) and the Ministry of Mines and Energy
a3770.speech: Have consistently reported that a large volume of minerals, particularly gold and diamonds, are produced informally and smuggled out of Liberia without any documentation, valuation, or taxation.

a3770.speaker: Industry experts and international studies
a3770.name: Industry experts and international studies
a3770.speech: Estimate that as much as 70 to 90 percent of gold produced in Liberia annually is not recorded in official export statistics, with smuggled gold alone representing a loss of between US$150 million to US$450 million per year.

a3770.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MoFD 2023)
a3770.name: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MoFD 2023)
a3770.speech: In FY2022/2023 the government projected revenue of around US$786 million, with a significant portion expected from the extractive industries.

a3770.speaker: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) (2021 study)
a3770.name: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) (2021 study)
a3770.speech: A 2021 study revealed that nearly 90% of gold produced in Liberia is smuggled out of the country each year, with the estimated value of gold lost through smuggling ranging between USD 159 million and USD 455 million annually.

a3770.speaker: Environmental health assessments
a3770.name: Environmental health assessments
a3770.speech: According to environmental health assessments, mercury exposure levels in several mining regions exceed World Health Organization (WHO) safety limits, raising concerns of a looming public health crisis.

a3770.speaker: Studies in mining zones
a3770.name: Studies in mining zones
a3770.speech: Have shown high rates of stunted growth, respiratory illnesses, and neurological conditions among underage workers.

a3770.speaker: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI), the World Bank, and Global Witness (reports)
a3770.name: Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI)
a3770.title: the World Bank, and Global Witness (reports)
a3770.speech: Multiple reports have highlighted the breakdown of regulatory authority in the mining sector and have urged urgent reform.

a3770.speaker: Field investigations, civil society reports, and testimonies from mining communities
a3770.name: Field investigations
a3770.title: civil society reports, and testimonies from mining communities
a3770.speech: Reveal that the Ministry of Mines and Energy has, in many cases, become a facilitator rather than a regulator of unlawful activity, with artisanal and small-scale mining licences frequently issued without proper vetting, environmental assessment, or community consultation, often to individuals or networks already known to be engaged in illegal extraction.

a3938.speaker: Associação dos Amigos do Museu do Cinema em Moçambique (AAMCM) (press statement)
a3938.name: Associação dos Amigos do Museu do Cinema em Moçambique (AAMCM) (press statement)
a3938.speech: In a statement, the organisation confirmed that Leão Lopes, author of Cabo Verde’s first feature film, “Ilhéu de Contenda”, will bring his vast experience to one of the central debates of the gathering, which brings together specialists from Cabo Verde, Germany, Angola, Brazil, Cuba, the United States, France, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique and Portugal ; “Among the most eagerly awaited moments is the debate ‘The power of cinema in political propaganda’, which will feature specialists from Cuba, France, Portugal and Brazil.”

a3980.speaker: Bloomberg
a3980.name: Bloomberg
a3980.speech: Reports that Mozambique’s Maputo port, a key chrome export hub, has stopped receiving cargo due to ongoing election unrest in the southeast African nation.

a3980.speaker: Maputo Port Development Co. (note to customers)
a3980.name: Maputo Port Development Co. (note to customers)
a3980.speech: “The Maputo Port Development Co., in coordination with customs and other relevant Mozambican border authorities, has taken the decision to stop reception of cargo at the Port of Maputo”, the company that operates it said in a note to customers Wednesday.

a3980.speaker: Dr Mike Masiapato, Border Management Authority Commissioner (South Africa)
a3980.name: Dr Mike Masiapato
a3980.title: Border Management Authority Commissioner (South Africa)
a3980.speech: Says they are monitoring the protests happening in Maputo, however they cannot predict when they will re-open the port. He was speaking to eNCA’s @pule_jones.

a4058.speaker: Beninese authorities (official order)
a4058.name: Beninese authorities (official order)
a4058.speech: On the orders of the Beninese authorities, officers of the central police station of Ouidah and forestry officials arrested the six suspected traffickers, with the technical collaboration of the Programme for Support to the Application of Wildlife and Flora Laws in Benin (AALF-Benin).

a4058.speaker: Law n°2002-16 of 18 October 2004 on the wildlife regime in the Republic of Benin (article 154)
a4058.name: Law n°2002-16 of 18 October 2004 on the wildlife regime in the Republic of Benin (article 154)
a4058.speech: provides that no one may import, export, re-export or trade in wild animals or their trophies and/or remains outside the permitted cases, and provides for this type of offence a fine of 300,000 to 800,000 CFA francs and/or imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years.

a4182.speaker: Mustafa Hashim, Somali swimmer
a4182.name: Mustafa Hashim
a4182.title: Somali swimmer
a4182.speech: “I hope that for now, they can focus on the youth getting into swimming.” ; “I believe my story can inspire others from underrepresented nations and show that athletes from any background with the right mindset can break through at the highest level.”

a4182.speaker: Mustafa Hashim, Somali swimmer
a4182.name: Mustafa Hashim
a4182.title: Somali swimmer
a4182.speech: “Hopefully, by LA 2028, I can go up against the much older athletes with a fight. I'll have grown a lot more physically, but from this meet I have gained a lot of experience and know what I want in the future as an athlete, hopefully making it to semis in Budapest 2027 in 100 breast and also being able to prove myself as a young athlete in Beijing 2026… It never hurts to dream big!”

a4182.speaker: United Nations
a4182.name: United Nations
a4182.speech: According to the United Nations, more than 7.7 million Somalis required humanitarian assistance in 2022, and the country ranks near the bottom globally in maternal health, gender equality, and childhood development.

a4256.speaker: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.name: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.speech: Said that "forgetting" of the population of Cabo Delgado, in the north of the country, by the state powers is one of the causes of armed conflict in the region ; "The cause of so much suffering has deep roots in the time when the population was forgotten."

a4256.speaker: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.name: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.speech: Notes that the violence in Cabo Delgado is inflicting "atrocities" on the population in the face of the inability of the Mozambican government to stop the action of the armed groups that are carrying out attacks in the province ; "Our hearts are filled with sadness to know of so many atrocities being practised in your province" ; Said the violence is forcing children to walk in the bush and seek refuge outside their homes, without food or any means of subsistence and with a bitter heart.

a4256.speaker: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.name: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.speech: Praised the solidarity of many families who live in safe areas, each of whom have given shelter at their home to more than 20 to 30 people forced to flee the armed conflict in Cabo Delgado province, and committed the CEM to mobilising aid from inside and outside the country for humanitarian assistance to victims of the armed violence in the province.

a4256.speaker: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.name: Episcopal Conference of Mozambique (CEM) (letter/statement of the Catholic bishops)
a4256.speech: The bishops praised the bishop of Pemba, capital of Cabo Delgado, Luiz Fernando Lisboa, for his constant alerts to the difficult situation in which the people of the province live.

a4256.speaker: Eric Morier-Genoud (@emorier), Twitter post
a4256.name: Eric Morier-Genoud (@emorier)
a4256.title: Twitter post
a4256.speech: "The Catholic Bishops of Mozambique wrote a letter to their brothers & sisters of #CaboDelgado. They express their solidarity, say they do not know what is the cause of so much suffering (though they recognise it has profound roots), and they publicly support the Bishop of Pemba."

a4326.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.name: Volker Türk
a4326.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.speech: Told Austrian public radio ORF that “It is clear that Israel can and must defend its people”, referring to the terrorist attack carried out on 7 October 2023 by the Palestinian Islamist group Hamas against Israel, but said that what Israel is currently doing is no longer justifiable by the right to legitimate self-defence: “When military actions are carried out, the international laws of war apply, which are also binding on Israel, but what we have seen in recent months no longer reflects respect for the fundamental principles of humanity.”

a4326.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.name: Volker Türk
a4326.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.speech: Said “I can no longer find words” to describe the “catastrophic situation” faced by the civilian population of Gaza, subjected to repeated forced displacement and without humanitarian aid for eight weeks, since the little that has arrived in recent days falls far short of the necessary volume ; added that since almost 80% of the Gaza Strip is now military territory where no one is allowed to remain, “we must speak of forced expulsion, which is deeply worrying”.

a4326.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.name: Volker Türk
a4326.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a4326.speech: Believes that Israel’s “friendly countries”, such as Austria, should pressure the government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to comply with international law ; earlier this month had already called for greater action by the international community to halt the current Israeli offensive, describing it as “equivalent to ethnic cleansing”: “Behind the systematic destruction of entire neighbourhoods and the denial of humanitarian aid, there appears to be an attempt to bring about a permanent demographic change in Gaza, in defiance of international law.”

a4983.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.speech: has urged President Bola Tinubu to immediately declare a state of emergency in Northern Nigeria, citing escalating insecurity that has devastated lives, crippled economic activities, and threatened national stability.

a4983.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF) communique
a4983.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF) communique
a4983.speech: In a communique signed by its spokesperson, Prof. Abubakar Jiddere, the forum expressed grave concern over the "relentless wave of violent attacks, abductions, and killings" across the region, stressing that the Federal Government can no longer afford to delay decisive action.

a4983.speaker: Prof. Abubakar Jiddere, spokesperson, Northern Elders Forum
a4983.name: Prof. Abubakar Jiddere
a4983.title: spokesperson, Northern Elders Forum
a4983.speech: "The NEF observes with deep regret that the security architecture remains inadequate, overstretched, and in some cases complicit through inaction and silence, leaving citizens vulnerable and helpless while eroding public trust in government institutions" ; warned that if the worsening situation is not urgently addressed, communities may resort to "self-help," which could trigger anarchy and undermine Nigeria's democratic stability and regional peace.

a4983.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.speech: cited recent incidents, including the August 19 attack on a mosque in Unguwan Mantau Village, where 27 worshippers were killed during morning prayers, the execution of 35 abductees in Zamfara State despite ransom payments, and deadly raids in Kaduna's Kauru and Kudan LGAs that left eight people dead.

a4983.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.speech: called on the Tinubu administration to adopt a multi-pronged strategy that includes declaring a State of Emergency in Northern Nigeria; deploying adequately trained, armed, and equipped security forces with clear rules of engagement to protect civilians and secure border regions; providing compensation, rehabilitation, and humanitarian assistance to victims, including displaced persons, in line with international humanitarian standards; strengthening border control and regional cooperation with neighbouring states under ECOWAS and AU protocols; and engaging international partners, including the African Union and United Nations, for technical and humanitarian support.

a4983.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a4983.speech: described the recurring atrocities as violations that could amount to crimes against humanity under international law if left unchecked, and pledged to continue engaging both domestic and international stakeholders to ensure victims receive relief and peace is restored in Northern communities.

a5044.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a5044.name: Marco Rubio
a5044.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a5044.speech: At a May 21 congressional hearing said, "No one has died because of USAID-" before being interrupted by Rep. Brad Sherman ; moments later responded, "That's a lie," as Sherman's staff held up photos of individuals said to have died after aid was cut.

a5044.speaker: Brad Sherman, U.S. Representative
a5044.name: Brad Sherman
a5044.title: U.S. Representative
a5044.speech: Interrupted Rubio at the hearing while his staff held up photos of individuals said to have died after aid was cut, and questioned the Trump administration's decision to dismantle USAID and freeze more than 90% of foreign aid programs.

a5044.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a5044.name: Marco Rubio
a5044.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a5044.speech: Maintains that the aid restructuring is part of a broader strategy to align foreign assistance with American national interests: "Foreign aid is not charity. It exists to advance the national interest of the United States." ; has called for a comprehensive review of all State Department spending and said future aid must demonstrate clear strategic benefits to the U.S., including in regions like the Horn of Africa.

a5044.speaker: Mariam Mohammed, mother of Babagana Bukar Mohammed
a5044.name: Mariam Mohammed
a5044.title: mother of Babagana Bukar Mohammed
a5044.speech: Said she had no money to seek alternative treatment after her 7-year-old son was turned away from a USAID-funded clinic in Nigeria that had received a stop-work order days earlier.

a5044.speaker: Mariam Mohammed, mother of Babagana Bukar Mohammed
a5044.name: Mariam Mohammed
a5044.title: mother of Babagana Bukar Mohammed
a5044.speech: Worries about her surviving son Umar, who also lives with sickle cell disease, and says the reopened clinic is her only hope: "My only wish is that these clinics stay open."

a5044.speaker: Nicholas Enrich, acting USAID global health administrator (internal USAID memo)
a5044.name: Nicholas Enrich
a5044.title: acting USAID global health administrator (internal USAID memo)
a5044.speech: Warned that the aid freeze could result in 12.5 million new malaria cases, up to 166,000 additional deaths annually, and 200,000 new polio cases. The memo was authored before he was placed on administrative leave.

a5044.speaker: Aid organizations
a5044.name: Aid organizations
a5044.speech: Warn that the human cost could continue to rise as the world's largest donor shifts its focus away from humanitarian needs and toward political strategy ; along with health experts, have levelled growing criticism at Rubio over the sweeping cuts to foreign assistance.

a5071.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.name: Badr Abdelatty
a5071.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.speech: Announced that Egypt has begun the training of 5,000 Palestinian police officers, who will be deployed under the control of the Palestinian Authority as part of the transition period ; "The precise list of members of the Palestinian police currently being trained in Egyptian camps, in collaboration with Jordan, has been finalised with a view to deployment in Gaza." ; added that "the deployment of the police elements and the question of the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip will be placed under the authority of the Palestinian prime minister, who will attend the Cairo International Conference for the Reconstruction of Gaza planned after a ceasefire is obtained."

a5071.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.name: Badr Abdelatty
a5071.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.speech: In his speech, insisted on Egypt's main objective: to return to the initial proposal of a 60-day ceasefire, including the release of certain hostages and Palestinian prisoners, as well as the unhindered and unconditional entry of humanitarian and medical aid into Gaza ; added that Cairo is working jointly with Qatar and the United States to revive a truce and end the war between Israel and Hamas.

a5071.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.name: Badr Abdelatty
a5071.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.speech: Told Sky News Arabia, regarding the demands made to Hamas to lay down its weapons, that the establishment of a political horizon in favour of the creation of a Palestinian state will be guaranteed by unity and by the exclusivity of weapons in the hands of the state.

a5071.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.name: Badr Abdelatty
a5071.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5071.speech: Criticised Israel's attempts to displace the Palestinians, affirming that "there is no legal or moral justification for expelling them from their land"; specified that such a scenario would prevent their return, adding that Israel simply wants to give them an "exit ticket" ; "A military occupation without the effective realisation of the rights of the Palestinian people will achieve none of Israel's objectives. It will guarantee neither the security nor the stability of Israel." ; "Israel's security will only be achieved through a serious response that includes the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people. And, first and foremost, the establishment of an independent and sovereign state." ; "Force will not lead to peace, but will increase the complexity of the regional scene."

a5081.speaker: Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) (statement)
a5081.name: Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) (statement)
a5081.speech: In a statement on Friday, the foundation said that since its inception in 2015, it has supported over 18,000 entrepreneurs across Africa, creating 1.5 million direct and indirect jobs and generating more than $4.2 billion in revenue.

a5081.speaker: Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF)
a5081.name: Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF)
a5081.speech: Says the selection process overseen by professional services firm Ernst & Young ensures an independent and transparent evaluation.

a5081.speaker: Tony Elumelu, founder of the Tony Elumelu Foundation and chairman of Heirs Holdings
a5081.name: Tony Elumelu
a5081.title: founder of the Tony Elumelu Foundation and chairman of Heirs Holdings
a5081.speech: "I believe that Africa's transformation will not be led by aid, but by empowering the next generation of African entrepreneurs— giving them the tools, the funding, the training, and the networks to build sustainable businesses that create jobs and drive economic growth." ; "Over the past decade, we have nurtured entrepreneurs from inception to success, scaling our impact across all 54 African countries. We have provided capital and also developed a robust monitoring and evaluation framework that allows us to track the progress of our entrepreneurs and measure their contributions to their communities and economies." ; "No other organisation is implementing entrepreneurship development at this scale across Africa. We have learned, we have refined, and we continue to improve, ensuring that African entrepreneurs—women and men—are at the forefront of solving our continent's challenges and creating wealth for themselves and their communities. Entrepreneurship is the key to Africa's prosperity."

a5081.speaker: Industry reports
a5081.name: Industry reports
a5081.speech: According to industry reports, venture capital funding in Africa fell by over 50 per cent in 2023 as global investors pulled back amid rising interest rates and economic uncertainty.

a5081.speaker: Fatima Diallo, Senegalese agritech entrepreneur and past TEF beneficiary
a5081.name: Fatima Diallo
a5081.title: Senegalese agritech entrepreneur and past TEF beneficiary
a5081.speech: Said the foundation's funding was crucial in launching her business, but securing follow-on capital remains a challenge: "I started my agribusiness with nothing but an idea. TEF changed everything. With the funding, training, and mentorship, I have now expanded across three countries and employ 25 people."

a5081.speaker: Mary Okeke, Nigerian fintech founder
a5081.name: Mary Okeke
a5081.title: Nigerian fintech founder
a5081.speech: "As a woman in the fintech industry, it was difficult to secure funding. TEF not only provided me with capital but also the confidence and skills to build a business that is now attracting international investors."

a5192.speaker: Council of Ministers of Djibouti, chaired by President Ismail Omar Guelleh (official communique)
a5192.name: Council of Ministers of Djibouti
a5192.title: chaired by President Ismail Omar Guelleh (official communique)
a5192.speech: Announced that the 16th sitting of the Council of Ministers took place on Tuesday 27 October 2020 and that the following texts were examined and approved: a draft law partially amending Law No. 154/AN/02 on the OPS and the general retirement scheme, abolishing the six-month time limit and extending voluntary insurance to dockers and other workers in order to ensure equal treatment among social insureds; a draft law transforming the National Tourism Office into a National Tourism Agency in the form of an EPIC, to give it greater flexibility and develop tourism as a driver of economic growth and job creation; draft decrees renewing the Boards of Directors of Radio Television of Djibouti and of the National Printing Office of Djibouti; and draft orders allocating a 5,500 m2 plot at PK13 to the Ministry of Women and the Family for a reception facility for street children, a 1,500 m2 plot in the South Port Zone for the headquarters of the Djiboutian National Olympic and Sports Committee, and a 22,000 m2 plot at the old Port of Djibouti to the company Ocean Indien Interconnexion O2I for a Data Center.

a5192.speaker: Minister of Higher Education and Research of Djibouti
a5192.name: Minister of Higher Education and Research of Djibouti
a5192.speech: Gave a mission report on the working visit he carried out in France from 19 to 22 October 2020.

a5192.speaker: Minister of Equipment and Transport of Djibouti
a5192.name: Minister of Equipment and Transport of Djibouti
a5192.speech: Gave an account of his participation in the 65th Ordinary Session of the Executive Bureau of the Council of Arab Ministers of Transport, held from 20 to 22 October 2020 in Alexandria.

a5259.speaker: Muhammad Albakri, IATA's Regional Vice President for Africa and the Middle East
a5259.name: Muhammad Albakri
a5259.title: IATA's Regional Vice President for Africa and the Middle East
a5259.speech: "Over USD 30 billion in financial support has been pledged to aviation and tourism in Africa. Some of this money has been allocated by governments, but far too little of it has reached its intended recipients. Governments and lenders need to urgently unchoke the bottlenecks so that the money can flow quickly, otherwise it will be too late to prevent closures and job losses. There will be no point re-opening the borders and skies if there is no industry left to speak of that is capable of supporting trade and tourism, which are the key components of any thriving economy."

a5270.speaker: Lusa (Portuguese news agency)
a5270.name: Lusa (Portuguese news agency)
a5270.speech: Writes that USAID's headquarters, in the Ronald Reagan building located a few blocks from the White House, has been closed since Monday, 03 February, after the agency's workers received an email asking them to stay at home.

a5270.speaker: The administration led by Donald Trump
a5270.name: The administration led by Donald Trump
a5270.speech: Claims that USAID is inefficient, that it unnecessarily subsidises equality and sustainability programmes around the world, and that its workers were "insubordinate" in the face of the order to suspend humanitarian aid.

a5270.speaker: The New York Times (cited by Lusa)
a5270.name: The New York Times (cited by Lusa)
a5270.speech: Reports that almost all of the 10,000 jobs will be eliminated and only a small group of 290 workers will remain.

a5277.speaker: Aboubaker Omar Hadi, President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.name: Aboubaker Omar Hadi
a5277.title: President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.speech: First wished the diplomat welcome and much success in his new mission, and gave a detailed presentation of all the infrastructure development projects under way and to come, including a presentation of the DPCS port community system, which he said has reduced port terminal response times from more than 72 hours to only 60 minutes.

a5277.speaker: Aboubaker Omar Hadi, President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.name: Aboubaker Omar Hadi
a5277.title: President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.speech: Stressed the advantages the new free zone and the Damerjog industrial zone offer for hosting American SMEs/SMIs so as to bring them closer to their outlets in East Africa, North Africa and the Middle East, noting that with a strategic position and modern infrastructure Djibouti is ideally located to become a trade hub for a vast regional 'hinterland'.

a5277.speaker: Aboubaker Omar Hadi, President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.name: Aboubaker Omar Hadi
a5277.title: President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (APZFD)
a5277.speech: Insisted on the need to close the gap in infrastructure investment in Africa, which today amounts to more than 107 billion US dollars per year, saying a more internally connected Africa would unlock the potential of landlocked economies, and that Djibouti's 15 billion dollars of infrastructure investment represents only a tiny percentage of the need ; urged the American diplomat to support this process of continental facilitation and integration through the infrastructure development fund, the more than 60 billion dollar International Development Finance Corporation (IDFC).

a5277.speaker: Christopher Canellakis, economic counsellor of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5277.name: Christopher Canellakis
a5277.title: economic counsellor of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5277.speech: Highlighted the importance of this system, which introduces total transparency into monetary transactions and speed in port and customs 'procedures'.

a5277.speaker: Christopher Canellakis, economic counsellor of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5277.name: Christopher Canellakis
a5277.title: economic counsellor of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5277.speech: Welcoming in passing the enormous investments in infrastructure development and the achievements already accomplished, reiterated his readiness to support this development process and to work on these areas of collaboration.

a5277.speaker: World Bank (estimates)
a5277.name: World Bank (estimates)
a5277.speech: Estimates that the infrastructure investment gap in Africa today amounts to more than 107 billion US dollars per year.

a5277.speaker: US State Department
a5277.name: US State Department
a5277.speech: Said the IDFC fund will combine the capacity of the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC) and USAID's Development Credit Authority "in order to offer innovative financial products making private capital available to developing countries."

a5571.speaker: Artur Ramos, Associate Director for Health Systems at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a5571.name: Artur Ramos
a5571.title: Associate Director for Health Systems at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a5571.speech: Explained that "the situation threatened the health of the population of Zambezia and jeopardized the progress of the province and the country towards the goal of controlling the HIV epidemic by 2030. We needed to act, and that was what we did."

a5571.speaker: Artur Ramos, Associate Director for Health Systems at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a5571.name: Artur Ramos
a5571.title: Associate Director for Health Systems at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a5571.speech: "Several hundred people benefit daily from the health services provided by these facilities, and we are certain that they can make a difference in improving health indicators other than those related to HIV."

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said the assessment of the IMF-supported reforms is positive: “The programmes have gone well, even with some delay in the so-called RMs, Reform Measures... the reforms are ambitious, complex, and sometimes interlinked” ; explained to the IMF Executive Board that the Fund normally deals only with the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, while here more ministries and agencies are involved, which requires difficult coordination ; said the government has the will to implement, that it has constraints, and that there has been progress; “I would say the programme has gone very well and Cabo Verde is considered a country with very good performance.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On why the programme has worked: “I have even asked the team to explain why the programme has gone well, because we have other countries where the programmes, unfortunately, have not gone so well. We attribute that, to a large extent, to the fact that the government has ownership of the programme. That is the ideal for any IMF programme... we support the programme, but the one who owns it is the government... the government takes the lead, it feels the programme as its own, not as something imposed by us.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said the adjustment has so far been very successful, given two brutal shocks – the post-Covid recession and the food and energy price increase following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine – with GDP falling close to 20% and by 33% at the worst moment, because of an economy excessively dependent on tourism ; said the recovery has been “very, very good”: 7% in 2021, 17% in 2022, 5.1% in 2023 and 7.3% in 2024, with the economy now 11% above the pre-pandemic level ; said the IMF advised that spending be maintained because it financed essential goods and services such as health and education, which prevented massive company closures and job losses ; said inflation rose from about 1.5% to close to 10% and fell back quickly, but food prices did not come down, and the minimum wage increase well above inflation is helping recover lost purchasing power ; called the maintenance of revenue collection as a share of GDP during the recession “really a great achievement by the DNRE.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said the speed of the recovery was surprising, since many other countries have not returned to their pre-pandemic trend ; said it was largely due to good policies but that the country also benefited indirectly from measures taken by partners, for example TUI, the largest tour operator in Cabo Verde, which benefited from German government support; “We take no credit, because the great majority of those measures came before our programme began.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said 2024 growth of 7.3% “was very strong and surprised everyone” – the IMF, which was projecting lower growth, and the government itself – and was clearly led by tourism and very strong services exports ; said that after the recent inauguration of the New Horizons hotel in Sal there are no large projects in the pipeline for the next two or three years, which is why the IMF projects a return to growth closer to the country’s potential of 4.5% to 5%.

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On mitigating risks, said there is still much potential to increase endogenous financing through continued fiscal effort to create fiscal space and resilience to a new shock ; noted reserves have returned to a comfortable level of close to six months of potential imports ; said there is great potential to diversify within tourism, which depends on a limited number of Northern European countries, and across the islands, which requires improving inter-island transport; “maintaining competitiveness, increasing diversification, both across sectors and within the tourism sector itself, and the creation of fiscal space are ways of trying to increase the resilience of the economy.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On the sixth review of the Extended Credit Facility, the 15-month extension and the increase equivalent to 30% of the quota: said that even with high growth the economy remains exposed and vulnerable to shocks, and that the IMF had to argue internally with its review departments and the Executive Board that a programme with additional financing made sense despite last year’s current account surplus; “there is now uncertainty as to whether or not that large amount of resources that was expected through the third MCC compact will be cancelled, and not only that, we have great uncertainty about the state of the economy at the global level.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said the country is “already at the limit” on tourism, with occupancy rates already high, and that imports are expected to rise with energy sector projects, so the surplus will become a current account deficit again, which makes sense for a country that still needs much investment.

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On debt sustainability, said the fall in the public debt/GDP ratio of close to 40 points of GDP is “spectacular” but that a projected level of about 105% of GDP at the end of this year “is still very high” and worries him ; said the main risks are that growth does not continue to be strong and the state-owned enterprise sector, whose high non-guaranteed debt could eventually be absorbed by the government ; said the IMF classifies external debt as at moderate risk of debt distress while the risk for public debt as a whole remains high.

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said the privatisation/concession processes could have three positive impacts – reducing fiscal risk, improving performance and competitiveness, and attracting investment – citing the airport concession, which in two years has produced many new airlines, routes and greater frequency, “a good experience that could be replicated in other areas.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On what to do with increased domestic revenue, said the positive primary balance that allows debt reduction “is very welcome, because the level is high and because the economy remains exposed to shocks”, and that it is very important to continue the fiscal effort to rebuild fiscal space.

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said Cabo Verde has a very favourable business environment on the macro side – low inflation, high growth, a fully open capital account, a fixed exchange rate regime giving investors certainty, and a solid financial system – but that on the micro side “it could be better”, with much bureaucracy that could be simplified to attract more foreign and domestic investment, citing the fast issuance of the NIF at the Casa do Cidadão as a good practice to replicate.

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On the global outlook: “I think we are still in an environment of great uncertainty and we will remain so for some time... each government has to make its own effort to try to overcome this environment, which is not very favourable. Uncertainty is not good for investment, and without investment there is no growth” ; said objective indices of uncertainty “are at very, very high levels. That is the reality, unfortunately.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: Said permanent dialogue between government and citizens is “very desirable” in the case of Cabo Verde, citing the visits of the prime minister and members of government to the National Assembly: “There is a good dialogue, an open dialogue, where all the relevant questions are put in a way that the public can follow.”

a6161.speaker: Rodrigo García-Verdú, IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.name: Rodrigo García-Verdú
a6161.title: IMF Resident Representative in Cabo Verde
a6161.speech: On whether commercial globalisation will return: “Very difficult to know. The truth is that I think at this moment it would be very speculative to say when the process under way will end.”

a6197.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO), UNICEF and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (joint statement)
a6197.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6197.title: UNICEF and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (joint statement)
a6197.speech: Have warned that rising outbreaks of measles, meningitis, and other vaccine-preventable diseases are threatening decades of immunisation progress; said the progress made over decades in reducing child mortality is at risk due to funding cuts, misinformation, population growth, and ongoing humanitarian crises; and are urging governments and donors to support global efforts to protect lives and sustain vaccination programmes.

a6197.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6197.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6197.speech: According to WHO, measles cases have been increasing since 2021, with an estimated 10.3 million cases recorded in 2023, a 20 per cent increase from the previous year; noted that in the past 12 months alone, 138 countries reported measles outbreaks, and 61 of them faced large or disruptive outbreaks; added that in Africa, meningitis is surging, with over 5,500 suspected cases and nearly 300 deaths reported in just the first three months of 2025 across 22 countries. “Yellow fever cases in the African region are also climbing, with 124 confirmed cases reported in 12 countries in 2024. This comes after dramatic declines in the disease over the past decade, thanks to global vaccine stockpiles and use of yellow fever vaccine in routine immunisation programmes. In the WHO Region of the Americas, yellow fever outbreaks have been confirmed since the beginning of this year, with a total of 131 cases in 4 countries,” WHO noted.

a6197.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) survey of 108 low- and lower-middle-income countries
a6197.name: World Health Organisation (WHO) survey of 108 low- and lower-middle-income countries
a6197.speech: Revealed that nearly half are facing disruptions to immunisation campaigns due to reduced donor funding; more than half also report challenges in disease surveillance, limiting their ability to track and respond to outbreaks. WHO highlighted that routine immunisation is struggling to bounce back from the setbacks of the COVID-19 pandemic, and that in 2023 around 14.5 million children missed all routine vaccinations, up from 13.9 million in 2022.

a6197.speaker: Catherine Russell, UNICEF Executive Director
a6197.name: Catherine Russell
a6197.title: UNICEF Executive Director
a6197.speech: Was quoted to have said that the global funding crisis is undermining efforts to vaccinate over 15 million vulnerable children in conflict zones. “We cannot afford to lose ground in the fight against preventable diseases.”

a6197.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6197.name: Donald Trump
a6197.title: US President
a6197.speech: In January, shortly after his inauguration, signed an executive order withdrawing the country from the WHO, citing political influence within the agency; he also paused all foreign aid assistance.

a6197.speaker: WHO, UNICEF and Gavi
a6197.name: WHO
a6197.title: UNICEF and Gavi
a6197.speech: Say vaccines save around 4.2 million lives each year, with almost half of those saved in Africa. “Joint efforts by WHO, UNICEF, Gavi and partners have helped countries expand access to vaccines and strengthen immunisation systems through primary health care, even in the face of mounting challenges,” they noted; they revealed that a new vaccine that protects against five types of meningitis is now being introduced, and stress that immunisation offers long-term economic and health benefits, with every $1 invested in vaccines returning about $54 in economic value.

a6197.speaker: Sania Nishtar, CEO of Gavi
a6197.name: Sania Nishtar
a6197.title: CEO of Gavi
a6197.speech: Noted that the outbreaks of highly infectious diseases concern the whole world, but “the good news is we can fight back”; spoke on Gavi’s next five-year strategy focused on expanding global stockpiles and targeting countries hardest hit by diseases like meningitis, yellow fever, and measles, but said this work depends on full funding. “Gavi’s upcoming high-level pledging summit taking place on 25 June 2025 seeks to raise at least US$ 9 billion from our donors to fund our ambitious strategy to protect 500 million children, saving at least eight million lives from 2026–2030,” she noted.

a6252.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6252.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a6252.title: President of Malawi
a6252.speech: Urged the newly appointed Senior Counsel to live up to the highest ideals of loyalty, integrity, and professional excellence, which he described as the foundational pillars for national transformation; warned that the honour of being named Senior Counsel comes with a lifelong burden of leadership by example: “You are now the example to the whole nation” ; “And I myself will rely on you for counsel and wisdom as I continue to lead this country without compromising these values.” ; “From now on, you cannot afford to drop the ball.”

a6252.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6252.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a6252.title: President of Malawi
a6252.speech: Rebuked the widespread belief that money, power, prayer, or foreign aid alone can fix Malawi's problems, calling for a culture of patriotic duty across all professions: “We need a nation of citizens who are loyal—not to individuals or tribes, but to the country, its laws, and their professional duty” ; “That loyalty, that unshakeable devotion to Malawi, is what I saw in you when I made these appointments.”

a6252.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6252.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a6252.title: President of Malawi
a6252.speech: Defined integrity as the refusal to cut corners or tolerate mediocrity, calling it the antidote to Malawi's chronic underdevelopment; on ability he was unequivocal: “It means that when the time comes to execute, you do not hesitate—and you do not fail.”

a6259.speaker: Barikis Yessoufou, speaking on behalf of all the young people of northern Benin
a6259.name: Barikis Yessoufou
a6259.title: speaking on behalf of all the young people of northern Benin
a6259.speech: “We, the young people of North Benin, firmly believe that with collective engagement we can overcome all the scourges that shake our regions. Among these we can cite the rural exodus of young people, the precariousness of life, social exclusion, cybercrime, the resurgence of alcohol and psychotropic substance consumption, intergenerational conflicts, and many others”; he stressed that it is possible to sow peace wherever they find themselves and that it is incumbent on them to support the local authorities in the development of their communities.

a6259.speaker: Brinille Ellis, representative of the United States ambassador to Benin
a6259.name: Brinille Ellis
a6259.title: representative of the United States ambassador to Benin
a6259.speech: After recalling the actions carried out by the US Embassy in Benin to fight violent extremism, expressed her admiration for the knowledge shared among the participants, with a view to creating a better and more inclusive future for Beninese youth: “The government of the United States is proud to stand by your side to build a safer, healthier and more prosperous Benin.”

a6259.speaker: Pascal Essou, Ombudsman of the Republic (Médiateur de la République) of Benin
a6259.name: Pascal Essou
a6259.title: Ombudsman of the Republic (Médiateur de la République) of Benin
a6259.speech: Stressed that peace and social cohesion are essential levers for the prosperity and development of territories; while welcoming the commitment of the participants, recalled that the first phase of the project made it possible to establish the bases of a constructive dialogue with the communal authorities of North Benin and to put in place a dynamic of active participation of young people in civic life, and that in its second phase the training and awareness-raising strengthened young people's capacities in advocacy and civic responsibility.

a6259.speaker: Pascal Essou, Ombudsman of the Republic (Médiateur de la République) of Benin
a6259.name: Pascal Essou
a6259.title: Ombudsman of the Republic (Médiateur de la République) of Benin
a6259.speech: Addressing the young people, expressed his conviction that they will resolutely put themselves at the service of community development and take a successful path towards ethical leadership, contributing voluntarily and consciously to the emergence of a more just and peaceful society: “From the feedback that has been reported to me, you are sufficiently equipped to contribute to the promotion of community dialogue”, inviting them to be the torchbearers of a new hope for successful mediations in their communities.

a6356.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.name: Soliana Shimelis
a6356.title: communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.speech: Currently, the Board is implementing pre-electoral operational plans for the upcoming national election, according to Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for NEBE, which has close to a four-billion-Br budget for the current fiscal year. “We're drawing out our communication strategy,” Soliana told Fortune.

a6356.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.name: Soliana Shimelis
a6356.title: communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.speech: The bid for the procurement of ballot boxes, ink and biometric voter registration machines have not been announced yet, according to Soliana. “We're still working on our operational plan,” she said.

a6356.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.name: Soliana Shimelis
a6356.title: communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.speech: “The used ballot boxes are still in Hawassa,” said Soliana.

a6356.speaker: Supporting Elections for Ethiopia’s Democracy Strengthening (SEEDS) 2019-2022 project document (UNDP, IOM, UNWomen, UNESCO, OHCHR)
a6356.name: Supporting Elections for Ethiopia’s Democracy Strengthening (SEEDS) 2019-2022 project document (UNDP
a6356.title: IOM, UNWomen, UNESCO, OHCHR)
a6356.speech: About 50 million people would participate in the upcoming election, according to the SEEDS project.

a6356.speaker: Sources from the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (anonymous)
a6356.name: Sources from the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (anonymous)
a6356.speech: For these procurements, the board floated a closed bid on October 11, 2019, due to time limitations, according to sources from the Board.

a6356.speaker: National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.name: National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a6356.speech: The Board announced that 98pc of voters in the referendum cast in favour of the referendum.

a6356.speaker: Dereje Zeleke (PhD), assistant professor of Addis Abeba University's School of Law
a6356.name: Dereje Zeleke (PhD)
a6356.title: assistant professor of Addis Abeba University's School of Law
a6356.speech: says that the Board seems to be progressing well in its preparation. "But the pertinent question isn't the Election Board's plans to have the election in May but the current political-social reality, which is the elephant in the room," said Dereje. "The government needs to assure citizens have a sense of peace." ; The political actors need to show a credible stance and movements for the upcoming election, according to him. ; The Electoral Board might have started the pre-electoral operational plan but drawing from past experiences, the feasibility of the election happening peacefully should be looked at and the pressing issues of the peace of the country should be assessed, recommends Dereje.

a6393.speaker: Dr. John Smith, security expert
a6393.name: Dr. John Smith
a6393.title: security expert
a6393.speech: “The Middle East conflict has far-reaching consequences... It fuels terrorism, destabilizes regions, and disrupts global economies.”

a6393.speaker: Dr. Fatima Al-Nauimi, Middle East analyst
a6393.name: Dr. Fatima Al-Nauimi
a6393.title: Middle East analyst
a6393.speech: “The conflict has created a power vacuum, enabling extremist groups to thrive,” notes Dr. Fatima Al-Nauimi.

a6393.speaker: Studies (unnamed)
a6393.name: Studies (unnamed)
a6393.speech: Studies show that economies across the Middle East and Central Asia are more affected by conflicts, in that even after a decade their income per capita remains about 10 percent lower; a year after the start of a violent conflict, countries in these regions lose about two percent in real GDP per capita compared to before the conflict.

a6393.speaker: Ambassador Mohamed Ali, African Union's Special Envoy
a6393.name: Ambassador Mohamed Ali
a6393.title: African Union's Special Envoy
a6393.speech: “The conflict's ripple effect reaches Africa's shores,” warns Ambassador Mohamed Ali. “We must address regional instability and economic concerns.”

a6410.speaker: Participants at the GNAPS Northern Region meeting
a6410.name: Participants at the GNAPS Northern Region meeting
a6410.speech: According to the meeting, some private schools, especially in rural communities, charge as low as five Ghana cedis per month due to economic challenges, and this is woefully inadequate for them to operate effectively; they are advocating for zero discrimination and urging the government to include private schools in its policies and programmes towards effective teaching and learning outcomes. Critical issues raised included high property rates, business permits, inspection rates and registration charges for BECE.

a6410.speaker: Private school owners and managers at the meeting
a6410.name: Private school owners and managers at the meeting
a6410.speech: Were bitter about the neglect of the government towards private schools; according to them, government must cater for both public and private school children to ensure that they all get quality education; they underscored the importance of private schools, adding that there are many communities where children will have no access to education but for these Low Fee Private Schools.

a6410.speaker: Alhassan Yamusah Salifu, Principal of Fatimah Farida School, Tamale
a6410.name: Alhassan Yamusah Salifu
a6410.title: Principal of Fatimah Farida School, Tamale
a6410.speech: "One of the GNAPS leaders raised an issue that I am happy about, he said at the district level, we should form an advocacy groups that can help raise these issues and GNAPS can not do anything without consulting the group. So I believe when that group is formed it will go a long way to help private schools."

a6410.speaker: Justice King Essiel, General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Private Schools (GNAPS)
a6410.name: Justice King Essiel
a6410.title: General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Private Schools (GNAPS)
a6410.speech: Said there are private schools in deprived communities that are doing well, not for economic reasons but for the sake of future leaders, and reiterated the commitment of GNAPS to knock on the doors of relevant stakeholders for collective change ; "All stakeholders who have represented have seen the need for us to collaborate and take away some of the barriers that discriminate against children in private schools. I think that is quite exciting and encouraging. We think that going forward we will be able to follow up on some of these things and hold them to their word."

a6410.speaker: Prof. Damascus Tuurosong, President of GNAPS
a6410.name: Prof. Damascus Tuurosong
a6410.title: President of GNAPS
a6410.speech: Said teachers at Low Fee Private Schools are not motivated to give their best because they are poorly paid: "In Kulkpeniduri, a community near Yendi, Rev. Inspector Inusah established Hope Education Complex for children. He is educating Ghanaian children at his expense. So why should such a school be denied Child support the that to attend for free. He uses his personal income to run the is extended to public schools just because it is a private school."

a6454.speaker: Recent Western policy briefs/reports on Chinese activities in Africa
a6454.name: Recent Western policy briefs/reports on Chinese activities in Africa
a6454.speech: Systematically attribute environmental degradation to “Chinese entities” while ignoring the multinational nature of African extractive industries; recommend that African countries implement comprehensive digital reporting systems; and recommend visa requirements specifically targeting Chinese nationals.

a6454.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China (at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation)
a6454.name: Xi Jinping
a6454.title: President of China (at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation)
a6454.speech: Emphasised China is ready to help Africa build “green growth engines”, with China pledging 30 green cooperation projects focused on green investments in energy and renewable technology sectors, along with $51 billion in financial support over three years.

a6454.speaker: China (announcement at FOCAC)
a6454.name: China (announcement at FOCAC)
a6454.speech: Announced it would “use development assistance to deliver 1 000 ‘small and beautiful' projects to improve people's livelihoods.”

a6454.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Foreign Affairs Minister of Lesotho
a6454.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a6454.title: Foreign Affairs Minister of Lesotho
a6454.speech: Proclaimed last year that the kingdom would have 100 percent renewable energy on its grid by 2028.

a6611.speaker: International Monetary Fund (July 2025 Staff Report on Tanzania)
a6611.name: International Monetary Fund (July 2025 Staff Report on Tanzania)
a6611.speech: Indicates that over 20,000 Tanzanians working directly and indirectly in the health sector will be affected by the USAID shutdown, and that 30,000 health workers who received supplemental income through USAID support are also expected to be impacted: "Most foreign assistance cuts have affected the health sector, both supplies and staff. For instance, USAID employed over 20,000 workers, both directly and indirectly (including CSO and community workers), mostly involved in HIV, malaria, family planning, and child health treatments. Another 30,000 health workers were paid by USAID to carry out additional activities beyond their official duties." ; Highlights that Tanzania was among the largest recipients of USAID support in Sub-Saharan Africa, receiving USD 400 million, equivalent to about 0.5 percent of Tanzania's GDP and accounting for approximately 40 percent of the country's total health expenditure, and estimates that around 0.2 percent of GDP per year in high-priority health spending will be affected by the funding cuts.

a6611.speaker: Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a6611.name: Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a6611.speech: According to the Ministry of Health, Tsh 93 billion was allocated to offset the anticipated budget shortfall.

a6611.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Tanzania's Minister of Health
a6611.name: Jenista Mhagama
a6611.title: Tanzania's Minister of Health
a6611.speech: "Through the coordination of the Prime Minister's Office, we have conducted a comprehensive assessment. We have reviewed what we currently have, what we have ordered, and what we expect to receive. We have already put in place a strategic plan for the short term, medium term, and long term," she told reporters on April 25, 2025, regarding the USAID exit.

a6611.speaker: Muhimbili National Hospital-Mloganzila (statement)
a6611.name: Muhimbili National Hospital-Mloganzila (statement)
a6611.speech: According to a statement released by the hospital, the surgery took approximately two hours, which is significantly shorter compared to traditional open surgery, which typically takes around four hours. The statement further explains that this new service, now available within Tanzania, offers several benefits to patients: reduced pain after surgery, minimal blood loss, smaller surgical scars, shorter hospital stays, and quicker wound healing times.

a6611.speaker: Dr. Richard Mliwa, specialist in gastrointestinal and liver surgery at MNH-Mloganzila
a6611.name: Dr. Richard Mliwa
a6611.title: specialist in gastrointestinal and liver surgery at MNH-Mloganzila
a6611.speech: Stated that this advancement was made possible through major investments by the government in medical equipment, healthcare infrastructure, and capacity building for medical professionals. "These investments have enabled the hospital to deliver proper and multidisciplinary care to patients using local expertise."

a6611.speaker: Bishop Josephat Gwajima, CCM member of parliament
a6611.name: Bishop Josephat Gwajima
a6611.title: CCM member of parliament
a6611.speech: Has called on the government and his party, the ruling CCM, to allow for minimal reforms and the participation of the opposition party, CHADEMA, in the upcoming election: "Chama Cha Mapinduzi has more than ten million members, so we have nothing to fear, so I advise that we decide to allow those from CHADEMA to be given minimal reforms—after all, they are just asking for reforms." ; "Let us try to identify which reform can be affordable at this moment, and give them a minimal reform, it doesn't take much time. Let's give them the reforms they want so we can go into the election with them." ; Argued that such a move is essential to ensure the legitimacy of power and to maintain calm and unity after the election, rather than having a divided country: "Whenever you think about political victory, you must also think about winning in a way that will make it easier for you to govern the country and bring development to the people." ; "Why should we enter into a game while the person we're supposed to play with isn't participating?"

a6611.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (2025 World Investment Report)
a6611.name: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (2025 World Investment Report)
a6611.speech: Reported that Foreign Direct Investment in Tanzania increased to USD 1.7 billion, the highest level recorded since 2014, a 28% rise from the USD 1.3 billion recorded in 2023, with the increase largely attributed to growing investments in infrastructure and the services sector; Tanzania's total inward FDI stock also grew from USD 19 billion to USD 21 billion, and Tanzania ranks as the eleventh largest recipient of FDI in Africa.

a6611.speaker: Jebra Kambole, Lawyer for CHADEMA Chairman Tundu Lissu
a6611.name: Jebra Kambole
a6611.title: Lawyer for CHADEMA Chairman Tundu Lissu
a6611.speech: Speaking outside the High Court premises in Dar es Salaam on June 17, 2025, stated that they had submitted their petition, while the prosecution had filed its defense supporting the use of secret witnesses, and that the parties now await the court's decision. "Mr. Lissu was not satisfied with the magistrate's ruling permitting witnesses to testify without revealing their faces, voices, documents, or names. He told us, his legal team, that he is not willing to have the case conducted in darkness."

a6611.speaker: Prosecution (affidavits signed by the Attorney General and Dar es Salaam Zonal Crime Officer SACP Faustine Mafwele)
a6611.name: Prosecution (affidavits signed by the Attorney General and Dar es Salaam Zonal Crime Officer SACP Faustine Mafwele)
a6611.speech: Argued that non-police witnesses should testify secretly due to alleged threats to their safety from Lissu's supporters.

a6864.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (social media post)
a6864.name: Donald Trump
a6864.title: US President (social media post)
a6864.speech: “Israel is not going to attack Iran. All the planes will turn around and come home, (...) Nobody is going to get hurt, the ceasefire is in force.”

a6864.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6864.name: Donald Trump
a6864.title: US President
a6864.speech: Speaking to journalists at the White House before leaving for the NATO summit in The Hague, admitted that Israel and Iran had violated the ceasefire he announced on Monday night, expressing disappointment above all with his ally Israel: “I’m not happy with Israel,” he stressed, while a message of his on social media demanded that Tel Aviv bring its pilots home: “Israel. Do not drop those bombs. If you do, it is a grave violation. Bring your pilots home. Now.”

a6864.speaker: Israel (government)
a6864.name: Israel (government)
a6864.speech: Claimed that it could not allow Tehran to develop nuclear weapons, and asserted that its adversary was “very close” to being able to produce nuclear weapons.

a6864.speaker: Iran (government)
a6864.name: Iran (government)
a6864.speech: Has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful.

a6864.speaker: Betzalel Smotrich, Israeli Finance Minister (social media post)
a6864.name: Betzalel Smotrich
a6864.title: Israeli Finance Minister (social media post)

a6864.speaker: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, supreme leader of Iran
a6864.name: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
a6864.title: supreme leader of Iran
a6864.speech: Vowed that he would not surrender.

a6886.speaker: A recipient from Baylor College of Medicine Children’s Foundation Lesotho (anonymous)
a6886.name: A recipient from Baylor College of Medicine Children’s Foundation Lesotho (anonymous)
a6886.speech: Said she was surprised to learn that her usual six-month dose will be cut in half. No explanation whatsoever.

a6886.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health of Lesotho
a6886.name: Selibe Mochoboroane
a6886.title: Minister of Health of Lesotho
a6886.speech: Said earlier this year that the country would not face any shortage of ART drugs ; has been in the forefront assuring Basotho that the HIV positive population would not be impacted by the suspension of the USAID ; was quoted as saying that the suspension of USAID will not impact on anti-retroviral therapy (ART) treatment supply as the country ‘has it under control’ ; at the commemoration of World Cancer Day reassured Basotho that they needed not to worry about the supply of treatment because “the Global Fund and government purchase the treatment” ; “There are 240 000 Basotho on Antiretroviral drugs. The government buys 73 percent of the drugs with the assistance of Global Fund securing 23 percent. Looking into matters, Global Fund is not affected by the orders.”

a6886.speaker: Ministry of Health of Lesotho (press statement)
a6886.name: Ministry of Health of Lesotho (press statement)
a6886.speech: Released a press statement essentially rubbishing allegations that there is a shortage of ART treatment, reassuring people living with HIV and the public that ‘there is no need for panic’: “The Government of Lesotho-MOH has adequate funding resources to ensure that a continuous and consistent supply of the life-saving HIV treatment (ART) is available at all facilities and in communities where HIV treatment is provided” ; the release also states that no facility in the country that provides HIV services has been shut down as a result of recent fund pausing or termination of HIV Programme on US funding ; stipulates that as from April 14 until further notice “people living with HIV who are clinically stable and reside in the country may be offered and dispensed three months clinical visits and HIV treatment”, and that people living with HIV who reside outside the country who are unable to attend three month appointments may be offered or dispensed 12 month clinical visits and treatment ; “The Ministry Health remains fully committed to addressing all public health concerns and reassures Basotho that HIV treatment will continue to be provided throughout the country.”

a6886.speaker: Patients from a number of ART outlets
a6886.name: Patients from a number of ART outlets
