a6886.speech: Have been complaining that their usual six months’ supply has been cut in half, done on grounds that there is a shortage in supply.

a6981.speaker: United Nations
a6981.name: United Nations
a6981.speech: According to the UN, this year's theme, "Better together: 80 years and more for peace, development and human rights," emphasises reinvigorating multilateralism, accelerating progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and addressing global challenges amid geopolitical shifts, technological advancements, and climate urgency.

a6981.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6981.name: Antonio Guterres
a6981.title: UN Secretary-General
a6981.speech: Warned that "impunity is the mother of chaos", and that cooperation is "a practical strategy for survival, not an act of naiveté", but cautioned that the principles of peace and progress are being eroded by war, inequality and climate chaos.

a6981.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6981.name: Antonio Guterres
a6981.title: UN Secretary-General
a6981.speech: Said: "Science says limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees by the end of this century is still possible. But the window is closing, emissions, temperatures, and disasters keep rising and those least responsible suffer the most. Renewables are the cheapest and fastest source of new power," and called for "stepped-up action and ambition, especially through strengthened national climate plans" ; said the G20, the biggest emitters, must lead, guided by common but differentiated responsibilities, and that all countries must lead by defining a credible roadmap to mobilise $1.3 trillion annually in climate finance by 2035 for developing countries.

a6981.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6981.name: Antonio Guterres
a6981.title: UN Secretary-General
a6981.speech: Said: "The choices we face are not part of an ideological debate. They are a matter of life and death for millions as peace is rooted in international law and is humanity's first obligation," stressing that "human rights are not an ornament of peace, they are its bedrock," and that these rights - social, economic, political, civil and cultural - are universal, indivisible and interdependent.

a6981.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6981.name: Antonio Guterres
a6981.title: UN Secretary-General
a6981.speech: Said that while "We have the solutions and tools", the fuel to achieve them through the shared roadmap of the Sustainable Development Goals needed financing, but aid cuts were wreaking havoc: "We know what we need, yet we are pulling away the very lifeline that makes it possible. To choose dignity, we must choose financial justice and solidarity."

a7008.speaker: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris, Nigerian film (Arseface) make-up artist
a7008.name: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris
a7008.title: Nigerian film (Arseface) make-up artist
a7008.speech: Speaking with Mwananchi, said she began this work in 2018, when she knew nothing about those types of make-up: "At first I did not know anything. I would watch American movies and ask myself how it is that a person's face is changed to become frightening, and how they come to appear with wounds" ; said that because of those questions she began wanting to know how people are transformed to have another appearance ; "At that time I knew how to apply other types of make-up, such as beauty make-up and editorial make-up. I had to start learning how to create frightening make-up through YouTube, because I had no money to study — it was very expensive" ; said she later managed to obtain training in applying that make-up in Canada, which helped her gain a broader understanding.

a7008.speaker: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris, Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.name: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris
a7008.title: Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.speech: Said the materials used to create that make-up are sold at a high cost, naming them as make-up silicone and powder.

a7008.speaker: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris, Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.name: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris
a7008.title: Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.speech: Explained that the biggest challenge she encounters in the work is that some actors set many conditions when make-up is being done on them: "I encounter challenges from actors; some have the habit of dictating to me what they want — that is, they are argumentative."

a7008.speaker: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris, Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.name: Abaeme Onyinye Stellamaris
a7008.title: Nigerian film make-up artist
a7008.speech: Says the work she does has surprised many people because even in Nigeria it is still not widely known, and said zombie creations attract her most: "Of all my works, I love creating zombies — in short, I love making a person look frightening."

a7208.speaker: Corporate Council on Africa (statement)
a7208.name: Corporate Council on Africa (statement)
a7208.speech: Made the announcement in a statement this evening that seven heads of state will attend the US-Africa Business Summit, which is also expected to attract more than 1,000 business leaders to Gaborone.

a7257.speaker: Duduzile Masuku, Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.name: Duduzile Masuku
a7257.title: Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.speech: Is of the view that, for the upcoming COP-28, African countries should consider the most critical issues, including the work program on the just transition pathway, which is of major interest for Africa.

a7257.speaker: Duduzile Masuku, Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.name: Duduzile Masuku
a7257.title: Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.speech: Observed that there is a lack of knowledge and skills when it comes to climate change issues, and that women are mostly affected by climate change as compared to their male counterparts, mainly because women are custodians of family unions within communities. “They are engaged in activities ranging from growing crops, fetching firewood all which are affected by climate change,” she said, noting that this negatively impacts them economically and socially, especially young girls ; “Women and girls should be engaged in platforms which can help elevate their capacity and capability offering knowledge and skills to mitigate these impacts of climate change through income generating projects geared at improving their welfare. Due to their vulnerability they are taken advantage of, resulting in victims of rape, gender based violence and other social ills.”

a7257.speaker: Duduzile Masuku, Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.name: Duduzile Masuku
a7257.title: Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.speech: Applauded Botswana for its efforts in combating climate change, saying the country is doing fine: “Botswana is generally doing fine in terms of showing commitment to climate change issues. Botswana has drafted a climate change policy which was adopted before Parliament, and through our NDC we have a target time to reduce emissions by 15 percent. The country has also strengthened climate change resources mobilization through mechanisms such as the 2021 Green Climate Fund among others.”

a7257.speaker: Duduzile Masuku, Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.name: Duduzile Masuku
a7257.title: Project Officer at Botswana Climate Change Network
a7257.speech: Acknowledged the International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) opportunity and shared that she learnt a lot on climate change issues. “I have learnt a lot especially how issues surrounding climate are addressed in the USA. While in Salt Lake we were told how the great Salt Lake is drastically drying up and one solution that they thought could solve the problem was getting water from the ocean. They have also found ways to turn their waste into gold, to ensure that they keep their surroundings tidy while also protecting their environment and benefit from the waste products.”

a7517.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, then President of Ghana
a7517.name: Nana Akufo-Addo
a7517.title: then President of Ghana
a7517.speech: Argued that ending dependence on foreign donors would not only lead to prosperity but also to "self-respect for our nation", when he launched his "Ghana beyond aid" policy in 2017.

a7517.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana
a7517.name: John Mahama
a7517.title: President of Ghana
a7517.speech: Sees reason for hope: "It sends a signal to Africa that the time has come for us to be more self-reliant."

a7517.speaker: Trump administration
a7517.name: Trump administration
a7517.speech: Says it will cut 90% of USAID's programmes globally, ending some 10,000 projects.

a7517.speaker: Charles Owubah, Action Against Hunger (NGO)
a7517.name: Charles Owubah
a7517.title: Action Against Hunger (NGO)
a7517.speech: "It's just a matter of time" before people die, in Ethiopia, where almost 16m people required food support in 2024 and funding for food aid has stopped.

a7517.speaker: Nicholas Enrich, top USAID official for global health
a7517.name: Nicholas Enrich
a7517.title: top USAID official for global health
a7517.speech: Outlined the effects of permanent aid cuts; he was placed on leave after sending memos warning higher-ups of the looming catastrophe. In one missive that was later made public he estimated that there could be 71,000 to 166,000 additional deaths from malaria and 1m more untreated children with acute malnutrition every year.

a7517.speaker: Linda-Gail Bekker, University of Cape Town
a7517.name: Linda-Gail Bekker
a7517.title: University of Cape Town
a7517.speech: Estimates that in South Africa, where PEPFAR accounted for 17% of the money spent on HIV treatment and prevention, there will be more than 500,000 excess deaths over the next decade as a result.

a7517.speaker: Moses Mutumba, head of a Ugandan NGO whose contract was ended
a7517.name: Moses Mutumba
a7517.title: head of a Ugandan NGO whose contract was ended
a7517.speech: Says there are already many cases of HIV-positive children not getting refills for their medicines.

a7517.speaker: Centre for Global Development, Washington (data)
a7517.name: Centre for Global Development
a7517.title: Washington (data)
a7517.speech: Data showing that in 16 African countries USAID funding is at least 1% of GNI, and an important source of foreign exchange.

a7517.speaker: Institute for Security Studies, South Africa-based think-tank
a7517.name: Institute for Security Studies
a7517.title: South Africa-based think-tank
a7517.speech: Estimates that almost 19m more Africans will fall below the World Bank's extreme poverty line by 2030 if aid from rich countries is permanently cut by 20%.

a7517.speaker: January Makamba, Tanzanian MP and former foreign minister
a7517.name: January Makamba
a7517.title: Tanzanian MP and former foreign minister
a7517.speech: Sees a paradigm shift on aid and is ambivalent about the change; he knows aid can do good but aid-dependence is bad. "As Africans we are not completely sad about the developments. This is what we have always been saying we want, to rely less on others."

a7517.speaker: Ken Opalo, Kenyan scholar at Georgetown University
a7517.name: Ken Opalo
a7517.title: Kenyan scholar at Georgetown University
a7517.speech: "Aid creates the wrong incentives for ruling elites." It leads policymakers to abrogate responsibility for their countries' own development and makes them more sensitive to donors than their citizens. Says aid partially causes "the atrophy of elite ambition" that has stunted economic development; aid can be palliative in the short term but, because of how it affects local politics, it is also corrosive.

a7517.speaker: W. Gyude Moore, former cabinet minister in Liberia
a7517.name: W. Gyude Moore
a7517.title: former cabinet minister in Liberia
a7517.speech: "You are so dependent on donor partners who pout if the minister himself doesn't show up. The smaller and poorer your country, the worse this is."

a7517.speaker: Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's founding president
a7517.name: Kwame Nkrumah
a7517.title: Ghana's founding president
a7517.speech: Spoke of a "new Africa" that would "show that after all the black man is capable of managing his own affairs".

a7517.speaker: Samuel Kalkoumdo, adviser to Burkina Faso's leader Ibrahim Traoré
a7517.name: Samuel Kalkoumdo
a7517.title: adviser to Burkina Faso's leader Ibrahim Traoré
a7517.speech: "We must try to develop without other countries…it can be a good thing and we will work hard to minimise the impact."

a7517.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a7517.name: Paul Kagame
a7517.title: President of Rwanda
a7517.speech: Often uses the word "mindset" and has said: "It is time to shake off the low expectations that have been attached to Africans and that we, to some extent, have accepted." Claims he has never been "a friend of [aid]", despite being "a beneficiary of it".

a7517.speaker: Jito Kayumba, adviser to Zambia's president
a7517.name: Jito Kayumba
a7517.title: adviser to Zambia's president
a7517.speech: Thinks aid cuts could spur African governments to spend more wisely; they are a chance "to build our own capacity, which is an issue of sovereignty and economic independence".

a7517.speaker: Afrobarometer (survey in 34 countries, 2019-2021)
a7517.name: Afrobarometer (survey in 34 countries
a7517.speech: Found that 65% of respondents wanted their countries to finance their own development, rather than rely on external loans; a majority held that view in all but four countries.

a7517.speaker: Bright Simons, Imani (Ghanaian think-tank)
a7517.name: Bright Simons
a7517.title: Imani (Ghanaian think-tank)
a7517.speech: Argues Africans may not be lamenting the aid cuts because the Western model of aid "has failed to live up to its own norms of accountability".

a7517.speaker: Study published in 2023 by academics at Lund University, Sweden
a7517.name: Study published in 2023 by academics at Lund University
a7517.title: Sweden
a7517.speech: Found that aid led to weaker fiscal capacity in African democracies, suggesting it got in the way of social contracts between the taxed and the taxer. "In effect, aid-dependent democracies become more autocratic," say the authors.

a7517.speaker: Ronald Osumba, Tony Blair Institute
a7517.name: Ronald Osumba
a7517.title: Tony Blair Institute
a7517.speech: "It's above all a capacity problem."

a7517.speaker: January Makamba, Tanzanian MP and former foreign minister
a7517.name: January Makamba
a7517.title: Tanzanian MP and former foreign minister
a7517.speech: Expects some systems to deteriorate or even collapse, but hopes the pain will be worthwhile.

a7517.speaker: Mavis Owusu-Gyamfi, African Centre for Economic Transformation (think-tank in Ghana)
a7517.name: Mavis Owusu-Gyamfi
a7517.title: African Centre for Economic Transformation (think-tank in Ghana)
a7517.speech: Argues the aid cuts were ultimately "coming down the line". She urges the continent to prioritise growth and transformation by integrating markets and moving beyond the extraction and export of raw materials; the end of an era in aid should prove a wake-up call. "And if our leaders don't wake up, then we have a fundamental problem."
